translations.text: On the Stones, by Epiphanius of Cyprus. Spoken by Epiphanius, bishop of the city of Constantia, which is the mother city of the island of Cyprus, which he spoke concerning the twelve stones.
To my lord, the honorable brother and sharer in the work, Theodore, the pious bishop: I, Bishop Epiphanius, greet you in the Lord.
He was giving a great gift of grace, and not receiving one, when the Lord of life asked to drink from the Samaritan woman.
For he himself was the spring of life, and he had come and sat down by the well, weary from the journey.
And he deemed her worthy of giving an answer, and he led her to the way of truth,
for the sake of which his coming in the flesh took place; and he generously distributed the gift to each individually and to all in common, since this human nature had been created by him.
Now, in unity, through the one incarnation, with one word and one will, everyone confesses forever and ever: This is the true Son of God,
who sought out his own creation. His disciples and servants would act in the likeness of this pattern: they would distribute gifts and receive nothing from anyone.
Truly, Elijah the prophet resembled his Lord: he asked from her who did not have even one measure of [?],
as though he had some need, he asked from the widow, because he wished by his blessing to fill that widow woman and to nourish her.
So too your Honor asks, rather, from this deficiency of my strength, because you wish to give me the gift of the grace that is with you.
Rather than receiving, you too have become like those who share in your work: through offering prayer to God you multiply my abilities for meeting your needs.

If there had been no running short of oil from the horn, from where would anyone have given? And if there had been no running short of flour from the jar of poverty, how could anyone have been able to be generous?
But your Honor has requested, as is written in this book, about the oracle, the plate of judgment,
which was adorned with stones one after another and was on the breast of Aaron the high priest.
Now you have wished that your Valor might know what the names of those twelve stones are, or in what places they are found,
or what power is in them, or how the names of the twelve tribes are written on them individually,
or how the counsel appeared in a manner befitting the worship of God, for by means of the names of the stones the high priest would discharge what the people needed.
But as I said before, all this difficulty was entirely beyond the power of my mind, and it was beyond my reach to find what so great a request asks,
just as it was for the widow woman because of her poverty and destitution.
But just as increase and multiplication came to the widow's store through the blessings of Elijah, and it abounded all the more, and as the Lord asked from the Samaritan woman for visible water,
and openly bestowed the counsel of those great gifts, so also me,
who am small in understanding and inferior in wisdom and knowledge and untrained in words, you have pressed to set my hand to this, and by offering prayer you have filled me too on every side.

Like the merchant enriched with all things, and like Elijah, who during that drought, by his care and by offering prayer, brought down the torrents of water, and like many other righteous men and prophets,
of whom you too are a son and disciple. Your honor has been made worthy to be placed on an equal footing with them.
You have received from them a surpassing abundance of wealth, as the Lord has granted it to you. And grant it to us all the more by your prayer.
Now I too will begin to set forth what you have commanded; but I beg your honor not to blame me for undertaking
what is a task beyond me, but rather to attribute it to my eagerness in obedience. And I will begin to set it forth beyond my strength.
And it is arranged in the first four, for the stones that were placed on the oracle of judgment, that tablet, were set in four places.
And the tablet of judgment itself was four-sided, a span in length and a span in breadth.
And in the first place was the first stone, the sardion, and after it the topaz, and then the emerald. And in the second, the carchedon and the sapphire and the jasper.
And in the third, the ligure, the agate, the amethyst; and in the fourth, which comes after all the others, the hyacinth and the beryl and the onyx.
These are the twelve stones on the oracle and tablet of judgment, each one arranged according to its place, arranged and fashioned and set.
1. The sardion stone. The sardion is called sardion for this reason, that it is found in Babylon, and its appearance is purple,
for it was named after the color and name of a fish: its color is that of the sardion fish, the color of blood.
When that fish is dried, its color becomes like blood. And because of that resembling appearance the name sardion was given to that fish.
It is found in Assyria. And the stone itself gives off brilliance and has a power of healing,
which physicians take and apply as a remedy, and with it they restore swellings and eruptions.
And also other wounds cut by the sword: they pour some of it on and smear it over them, and by that anointing the wounds are healed.
There is another stone, which is called sardion-onyx. And some call it molochas because of its color and its power, which bears a likeness to the mallow.
For those who drink of it, it [?] the belly and keeps it loose. And its color itself is like that of the green plant.
And the more moisture it draws to itself, the more it makes its greenness shine, especially in the season of summer and on the days of fullness.
There is also another stone similar to these, which is called sardak, which has altogether a certain color of whiteness, like the akad stone, and it changes.
It is itself somewhat, as they say, evil, and it was called the pacifier.
2. The topaz stone. The appearance of the topaz stone is purple. And it resembles the stone that is called carchedon.
And that topaz stone was found in the city called Topaze, in the land of India.
And it was found in this way: stonemasons were cutting stone, and it was found inside one stone that they were cutting.
When they saw the beautiful color of that stone and its marvelous appearance, they took it up and sold it to certain merchants of Alabastra,
which is near the region of the Alabastrians in India; and the Alabastrians received from them some small payment and gave the topaz stone.
Those Alabastrians brought it to the city of Thebes, which is in Egypt, and sold it for a far greater price than what they had given.
Those Thebans offered it as a gift to the king who was in that city at that time, and he received that topaz stone and set it in his crown, right at the middle of the forehead.
And this stone has a power proven by testing, as follows: when it is ground on a physician's grinding stone, it does not give off purple water in the grinding, like its own color.
Instead its groundings are the color of milk, white. And it fills many vessels, as many as the physician wishes,
who gives the stone to be drunk; and when he has collected the groundings, he weighs the stone, and it has not diminished at all, but keeps the same equal weight.
And its shape all around, whatever it was, it keeps the same and is not diminished, and it is of benefit to diseased eyes.
And if anyone drinks it, it is of benefit to those who suffer from dizziness and to the [?].
And if anyone eats the lake-grape and is harmed [?] by its bitterness, physicians give him the groundings of this stone to drink and cure him.
3. The emerald stone. The emerald stone and agate are green in appearance.
But there are distinct differences in their color: for the emerald gives off brilliance, while agate is only green.
And some call these stones Neronian, and others Domitianic. And the Neronian has a strong greenness of its own, and its appearance is beautiful.
And they call it Neronian for this reason: they say that King Nero brought green-colored oil, which is at Libertia [?].
And others say that he collected almond milk and many other green colors as well, and irrigated the mountains,
where there was an abundance of boulders and of [?] stones. And others said: he took Domitianic oil and poured it into vessels of copper.
And when that oil stands for a long time in those copper vessels with the dross of the copper, the oil turns green, and with it they irrigate the mountain whose stones are green in color.
And when that oil reaches them, it becomes much greener and shines brightly.
And it was called Domitianic because Domitian, son of Vespasian, was king in those times.
These were the ones who captured and laid waste Jerusalem. These kings, Nero and Domitian, were self-loving, given to adornment, and arrogant.
In their days they labored in this way to find those precious stones. And others say: it is found in the land of India and is brought from there.
And some say: it is found in Ethiopia, in the river Pishon, as the Scriptures testify to these words of ours, that the emerald is found in the river Pishon.
And it says: "The river Pishon encircles the land of Havilah. There is the precious stone agate, the carbuncle, and the kapoet [?]."
And the river Pishon is called Indus in the language of the Romans, while the Bariminians [?] and Bogians [?] call the Pishon the Ganges.
But the earlier Roman narrators spoke of the river Ganges, which encircles the land of Havilah, and they say that Havilah is outside India and that it runs alongside Ethiopia,
which is near the setting of the sun, for this is the great Ethiopia, and it runs alongside Ethiopia and joins the Ocean.
For a stone of crimson color is also found in it, when the movements of its courses take place in torrent-filled [?] places.
The Ethiopians have settled in such places. But as for the green stone, which in "Genesis" was called agate, the translator Aquila
called it neither agate, nor green, nor emerald; but because he was very knowledgeable in the language of the Hebrews and its interpretation,
he found, in a certain place, that the name of that stone was written as bdellium, concerning which the seventy translators said:
"From there comes the agate stone," which is green in color, which the Greeks call prasinos, and which in the language of the Georgians is called green-colored.
And Aquila says: "There is the bdellium stone," and bdellium is translated "incense of fragrance," which that river brings from the land of India.
For there are also many other stones like the emerald, each of which someone found separately, and there is one that is by nature brilliant and green.
And there is one that is hard and one that is soft. There is one that is found in Ethiopia and one in the land of India.
We must also state this: which mountain it is that Nero waters, or which it is that Domitian waters, or in what country it is.
That mountain is in the country near the Red Sea, when someone wishes to travel by ship to the land of India.
For there are various countries of India, and in those many countries there are nine kings, and these are the names of those countries and their peoples:
the Alabastrians, the Homerites, the Aximinians, and next to them the Dulatians, the Bogitavanians, the Asabians, the Dibenians, and the Lelediben.
But now they have also changed to other names because of the many who came as strangers from many places.
In the first place, the Hindobenon: these went from the country of the fish-eaters; the Sirindibenians: these came from the land of Havilah.
But let us also speak of other places, wherever it may be fitting. Now, however, let us speak of the mountain where the emerald stone is found: it is under the rule of the king of the Romans.
The name of that mountain is Zmurian, and it is like a forest of its own, and it lies opposite Berenice, the point of departure for India.
When someone goes to the Thebaid, it is still distant from the sea by about the run of a single ship,
which is only about eighty miles, and it is near Berenice, close to the places named "Elephant's Bones."
And the people of the Blemmyes hold it, who also hold many other places.
And now foreign peoples of the pagans cut out that emerald stone and take it for trade.
And the power of its color is this: like a mirror, it shows from within, and it produces foreknowledge through that manifestation.
4. The jacinth stone is jacinth in color, brilliant like fire, like a panak [?] in its crimson redness.
It is found in the regions of the Carthaginians, who are Libyans, in the place called Africa.
And others have said that this stone is found in this way: its brilliance does not appear by day,

but at night it burns from afar like a candle and gives off brilliance like a live coal, and like a kindled furnace which is immediately subdued by something being placed upon its flame, and like a coal it appears mixed with white.
And by that shining forth they see that stone from afar. In some places it is the color of an ember, and in some places like a blaze.
And by seeing it in this way they recognize that stone and go to it, and they find it by the brilliance it gives off.
And whoever carries it and does not know what stone it is carries it on the outside and not within his clothing,
and by the radiance of that light its brilliance reaches distant places. For this reason it is called "ember," because of such light and brilliance.
And its power is this: when someone rubs that jacinth stone on a grinding stone and someone drinks what has been ground, it awakens the soul to righteous words;
and if anyone holds it in his mouth, he weighs out upright and just judgment. This stone resembles that ember only slightly, and it falls down like fire.
There is also another stone like this one, which was called carchedon. And it resembles those stones in color, for they are found in the same places.
But if it is thus something marvelous to behold, of which the divine Book [?] speaks, which comes out of the river Pishon, this stone is also found in Africa.
And it is found in this way: for the river Pishon joins the sea in those places in the direction of Bghuaria [?]; in the west it joins the Ocean, for the Ocean surrounds all the ends of the sky.
And on the western side the river Pishon joins the Ocean, near that country of the Libyans, for thus says the divine Book:
"A river went out from Eden and was divided into four heads. The name of the one is Pishon. This is the one that encircles all that land of Havilah.
There is gold, and the gold of that land is good. And there are anthrax, the scarlet stone, and kapoet [?]."
5. The Sapphire Stone. The stone that is called sapphire is of a purple color.
Like purple, that sapphire stone appears dark and black in color. And there are also many other stones similar to sapphire.
One is called by the name basilike, and others chryse [?] and tige [?], which are not so fine to look at: their colors are somewhat faint.
And as I suppose they have said, they are in India and Ethiopia, and they stand arranged in a row in that idol-temple of Dionysus,
although what they say is not credible, that there are three hundred and sixty-five steps.
And all of it is of sapphire stone, and each single step is itself of sapphire stone, and they are fitted to one another with chains,
for this is a marvelous stone of kings, beautiful and desirable to behold. For this reason some have called it by the name alexiponon.
And the power of that stone: when someone prepares [?] what is ground from it and mixes it with milk, it heals phakli [?], swelling, eruptions, and tumors.
It is written in the Law of Moses, when he saw on the mountain, that "there stood under his feet the body of the sky, of those sapphire stones."
6. The Jasper Stone. Jasper is a stone, and its appearance is like emerald.
And it is found opposite, near the river Thermodon and near Amathus, not the one that is in Cyprus.
For by nature there is much of it, that which is called amathusion, whose appearance is of a green color,
like that of emerald, but it is slightly dark in appearance, and from within its green color it gives off something like copper.
And those who wish to adorn themselves make themselves beautiful with it, as is said in the fables.
There is also another stone, redder than the waters of the sea and darker than flowers.
There is also another stone, which is found in the caves of the mountains of Sidesia, which is in Phrygia.
Its color is that of blood, and it is brighter, like the color of the root of pearl [?], and like the color of wine; it resembles the amethyst stone.
And it is more reddish, and it is not of one color nor of one power. And there is another which is brighter, resembling flame and smoke, and whiter and more brilliant still.
And some, drawing on fables, say that the stones do something notable.
And this is found in the borders of Kartli and in Gorgan, and in the land of the Caspians, where there are tribes.
Next, there is another jasper, not very brilliant and green in color. And there are particles [?] within that stone.
And again there is another jasper as well, which is called upavlios [?]; it resembles the stone and the peruli [?] of the sea, and as if someone had mixed blood with milk,
And as the Masqatians [?] drink, and in the way they relate to us, those who find these in villages or on estates have a certain fear laid upon them.
7. The stone ligurion. How ligurion was found, we could nowhere discover:
neither among those who undertook to describe its nature, nor among those others, the ancients, who turned their attention to it.
But we have heard its name, which is called ligurion.
Those who spoke the true and established language call it ligurion, and, as I think, that ligurion,
just as we have found names changed in the divine books, for they called the emerald stone 'green-colored' and gave other names to other names, and they named the ligurion lagurion.
Although the places where it was found are also hidden from us, it has come to our mind that it is found in the Thebaid, concerning which they have said
that there are cliffs there, and that in those cliffs the stone is quarried. And that stone is called Asclepion, of the king of the Egyptians.
And in that stone there are what look like veins traced out, resembling the stone called kerinon, and those veins are green in color.
And we are to understand that those veins are in the cliff from which the stone is quarried.
And when that stone is quarried out of the cliff, it appears exceedingly beautiful, with veins mingled through it.
And when someone truly investigates that name, ligyros is the name of an animal which is called ligyron, which has the color of the wild ox, resembling a red heifer.
And at the tip of its fly-whisk [?] it has hair in a tuft, and it bursts out green in color, from which it was also named ligyroz, which in turn is translated ligurion.
But I marvel, as I have searched out with labor from the divine books, how with various ornaments of beauty, as for a king,
they made the crown and the tunic of the priest, and how these precious stones were found, and they brilliantly set this jasper as an adornment,
all the more the one in which there was the power, through the prior manifestation of signs, which we have also mentioned before.
I speak of the jacinth and the emerald [?], the amethyst and the agate and the beryl and the carchedony; and as for the names of the gems, no one anywhere could mention the jacinth gem,
for it is most marvelous and precious, and, as I suppose, the one they call ligure is called jacinth in the divine books.
And the jacinth gem is many-colored, and thus it is more precious than many gems, for it is spoken of in the divine books too:
that "they made [it] from the ornament of jacinth and from purple." We find in the color of the jacinth gem a purple hue, the color of honey, and the color of [?].
And there is another gem like it, sea-colored; and another, which they call rhodios; and another, which they call natibos [?]; and another, like the color of water, which they call kauniēos [?].
And there are many other gems too, which resemble this gem in brilliance, and others of various colors.
And these gems are found in the interior regions of the pagans, who are the Scythians.
And as those of former times said, Scythia is in the regions toward the north, in which regions are the peoples of the Etelians [?] and the Huns,
the Larians [?], and the Aranians [?], as far as Germany and the Amazon land, and beyond them there is a desert, which they call Great Scythia.
There is a certain valley there, great in depth and dark, into which no man can possibly descend.
And mountains surround it, whose summits are firm rock, and on that side it is sheer from below right up to the very top of those mountains.
If anyone should wish to approach and look down, it is not possible to see the jacinth,
for because of the great depth, darkness covers its floor, and there are great terrors; and in that depth, in the dark abyss, they say, is the jacinth gem.

And the men who go by command of the rulers to find and bring back the jacinth gem, since they cannot descend into that valley because of its depth, and out of fear of the kings' command strive to find the gem,
then they take lambs and slaughter them, flay the head, and throw them into that depth, and the gem sticks to the flesh.
As they say, the eagles that nest in that rock, in anxious concern over the hunger of their young, catch the scent of the carrion.
They descend into those abysses, into that unseen darkness, and carry the lambs' carcasses up to the tops of those mountains; and when the eagles have eaten the lambs' carrion,
the jacinth gem remains right there in that place on those mountains. And the men who have come to find the jacinth gem
keep watch and observe the place, and they sit on the tops of those mountains, observing the place where the eagles eat the carrion.
And they sit and watch until they have eaten. And when they fly up and go far away, then they go over, gather up the gem, and clean it of the carrion
that the eagles brought up, and they carry it away and hand it over to the rulers who sent them.
And in this way they find the jacinth, which is itself many-colored and precious. And this power is in it:
Whenever someone takes that gem and places it on a burning coal, the coal goes out, and the gem itself suffers no harm, nor does it even grow hot.
And not only this, but if someone wraps it in a linen cloth, or in anything else, and places it on a coal, that wrapping itself suffers no harm from the blazing fire.
But the cloth in which the stone was wrapped and laid upon the coals is not harmed even slightly by the fire, even though the coals are blazing fiercely.
And they also say this: that when women are giving birth and this stone is brought near them, it gives them endurance and easy childbirth; and it dispels the [?] of the customary [?].
8. The agate stone. The agate stone: how very white its color is, although it is inferior to hyacinth; but it is wonderful to behold and entirely white all around,
like ivory and like marble. And this agate stone is found in the region of Scythia.
And the power and virtue that is in it, in the agate stone, is this, the appearance of its color: in appearance it is like a lion.
And they mix its kind [?] with water and smear it on wounds and on the bite of beasts, and it heals the wound, the bite of the asp.
Of [?]. And it is customary to say this, that the agate stone is the color of a lion.
9. The amethyst stone. The amethyst stone blazes all around like a kindled fire, and within it is a radiance of white color.
And it also has the color of wine, and at the middle of the stone it gives off greater brilliance.
And it is found in the borders of Libya. And there is one kind that is purer than hyacinth, and there is another kind that resembles the root of a pearl.
And it is in those places of Iosite [?], which is Libya, whose territories extend as far as the sea.
And the name was given to it in keeping with its power and virtue, for those who look at it become drunk.
And by means of it winter and rain are known in advance, from the moisture of the winds.
10. The scarlet stone. The scarlet stone, concerning which some say 'scarlet', is called bwirwil [?], for it has a golden color around it, like a belt, as a vein.
And it is found in the pit that is in the rock of Ezramenidos [?] of Babylon.
And Babylon and that pit of the rock were called Achaemenida, for they say that the father of King Cyrus was called Achaemenes, as some recount to us from writings.
There is also another stone, of scarlet and green color. And the power of its virtue is this:
When physicians give its powder to drink, it benefits those whose stomachs are nauseated and those whose bowels are stirred up.
11. The beryl stone. The beryl stone is itself white, like a cloud; something like pure water appears to be moving within it, and it is darker than the amethyst stone and purer than hyacinth.
And it is found at the foot of Mount Taurus. And when someone holds it up toward the sun, it flashes out in the color of manna, like a grain of wheat.
There is also another beryl, which resembles the pupil of a dragon's eye. And there is also another beryl, which resembles wax.
And there is another beryl, which appears as if wrought by hammering, and this is found at the crossing of the Euphrates River.
12. The onyx stone. The onyx stone: its color is red mixed with darkish.
And the brides of rulers adorn themselves with it in rejoicing, and for sovereigns and the rich they make drinking cups from this onyx stone.
There are also other onyx stones similar to this one, whose color is like a honeycomb.
And some say that this stone is formed in waters by congealing.
And the stone was given the name "nail" [onyx], as the interpreters say, because a person's nail resembles marble, and through its blood it gives off a reddish color.
And some, having found marble stone in pure places, gave it instead the name "nail-stone" because of the purity and smoothness of that marble.
These are the twelve stones that are written on the board of judgment, which was commanded to be placed on the breast of the priest.
I, in this my weakness, what I have found set forth by the natural philosophers, the distinctions and the powers that are in them, and also the places
from which they come or how anyone may be able to find them, I have applied my mind to the labor according to our ability,
and because of your command I have boldly arranged and written down the names of these stones one by one.
I will now begin to set forth, according to my ability, the power and form of those stones one by one: on which stone the name of which tribe was written,
or the likeness of which tribe and clan it shows us, or what meaning and interpretation is in them.
1. The sardion stone. The sardion stone is the first on the square, the oracle, and that board of judgment.
On it was written the name of Reuben, the firstborn son of Jacob.
And this is the meaning and interpretation of that stone: the sardion stone is found in Babylon, and Babylon is translated as "division" and "scattering."
Truly, rightly, and in very truth was the name of Reuben written on that sardion stone, which is found in Babylon,
for just as in Babylon, in the affair of the tower, scattering and division befell that first generation,
so also, because of his sins, there befell Reuben the scattering and division of his lamentations [?] through that error of lust, and he was cursed by Jacob his father.
There is, moreover, also a great restoration in that sardion stone, for by its ground paste healing is brought about for wounds,
just as Reuben revived from that wound of his sins, for he acted well toward Joseph, his brother, and rescued him from being killed by the brothers.
And Moses, having come to the blessings of the sons of Israel, spoke thus:
"Let Reuben live and not die," for the patriarch Jacob had cursed Reuben and said: "You defiled my bed; like water, may you not boil up."
And as for what he said, "May you not boil up," in Hebrew it says, "May you not boil over, may you not flourish."
But Moses, in those blessings, spoke over Reuben as one who had received that authority from God, as high priest and prophet and as one informed by the Spirit of it,
namely, that he did that good deed for Joseph. He knew both that sin of Reuben and, after that sin, his righteous conduct as well,
and he forgave that sin of Reuben; as high priest he blessed him and said: "Let Reuben live and not die."
These are the figures and interpretations of the meaning of that sardion stone and of the writing of the name of Reuben upon it.
Let it be enough for us to have said this: let us come only as far as here, and let us set forth the meaning of the second as well.
2. The topaz stone. After this comes the topaz, which is the second stone, on which is written the name of Simeon.
This stone, as I said above, is the topaz. The stone comes from the city of Topaz, and that city is in India, and this topaz stone is beautiful and wonderful to look at,
and brilliance bursts forth from it like a burning coal. The stone is reddish. Stonecutters found it and sold it to Alabastrene merchants.
They took it to the city of Thebes and received a greater price than what they had given for it.
The Thebans received that topaz stone and presented it to the king who was in the city of Thebes at that time.
And that king received the topaz stone and set it in his crown, right at the middle of the forehead.
And the interpretation of the stone is this: Judas Iscariot, who became the betrayer,

put his hope in that precious stone and for a long time was with his Lord as a sharer in his life, yet wickedly, through the desire of the love of silver and through covetousness, he failed to search it out.
Rather, through that wickedness and covetousness he became foolish and inexperienced, like those stonecutters.
And he did not grasp the knowledge of that precious stone, our Lord Jesus Christ, but sold the Lord to those scribes and Pharisees,
who were of the kindred of Simeon, and the price of whom, the Son of God, could not possibly be paid in a sale.
The betrayer Judas delivered him to the chief priests and received some small price, which was this: he gave him up for thirty pieces of silver.
But those scribes and Pharisees and chief priests, with great envy and pride and [?], gave that precious stone, the Lord of all creatures, into the hands of a layman,
into the hands of Pontius Pilate, just as those Thebans did. And they crucified the Lord of life.
This is the one whom they offered as a gift to the Church, as the Thebans did to that crowned ruler.
And just as that king received the topaz stone and set it in the crown, right at the middle of the forehead, so also the Church,
the wife of the great King, the Son of God, received him who was rejected by the builders,
as a king places on his head a crown and diadems, and with pride is sealed with that sign of life [?] in the middle of his forehead.
For Christ is the head, and the Church is his member and the bride of that great Bridegroom, who is proclaimed at all times by the sign of the Cross.

And she has taken it up and holds it with great joy, and in depicted form she is sealed in the middle of her forehead, just as the crowned ruler received the topaz stone and set it in the crown, right at the middle of the forehead.
And as we said, when a physician takes that stone and grinds it with water on his implement, it does not give the color of its ground paste in keeping with its own purple hue,
the paste with which they restore the sick to life; rather, its paste is white as milk. And as much as anyone wishes,
he fills vessels with the paste from the topaz stone and performs many healings of sicknesses and of painful eyes.
And whatever its measure around was, it retains that same amount. And when it is weighed, it is not found diminished, but remains just as it was,
Just as it happens that many vessels are filled with its ground powder, by which many ailments are healed,
we now see the same pattern in the blood of Christ. And healing comes about for the souls and bodies of all who receive it.
For as to the blood that is from the body of Christ, we who are healed by it do not become blood of a purple color,
but it changes our bodies and souls into holiness and whiteness, when it cleanses the dross of sin from us and we become like snow and wool.
As it says: "Who are these who come up from the wilderness, who are white as snow and like a washed flock?"
And like the topaz stone, which gives off its outflow and yet remains in its own nature,
so also our Lord was in no way diminished by his appearing in the flesh, nor did he lack anything,
but, tested in all things and entirely complete in this nature of ours, he passed through every affliction,
except sin, and he sanctified and gave life to the whole of this humanity, and we all receive from him the Holy Spirit and power and wisdom and knowledge.
All of us who believe in him receive very great signs from him, and nothing is lacking to him, as the divine word says by the mouth of John the Evangelist:
"We have all received from his fullness." This is the precious stone and the seven-eyed pendant stone,
which fills all with the illumination of its knowledge and is itself in no way diminished in the light of its radiance, but stands and remains in its own essence.
Just as the light of one lamp kindles thousands and myriads and more lamps, and by spreading its light over them and illuminating them all is not itself diminished in its own light,
nor does it lack anything, so also Christ has enlightened from his fullness,
and that fullness is diminished by no one and lacks nothing, but remains in its own fullness and fills and enlightens others.
3. The emerald stone. The third stone is the emerald, on which was written the name of Levi.
For the tribe of Levi held the priesthood, and they were called Levites,
who were descended from Merari and Kohath and Gershon. This wonderful tribe was written on the emerald stone, for the emerald is a green, shining stone.
Many of that tribe who held the priesthood were weak and frail from great labor and fortitude, blanched,
pale and greenish in color, and through their love of labor their illumined soul shone with the graces of the Godhead.
For John too was of that tribe of Levi, enduring in labors in keeping with the fortitude of that tribe, and by his holy virginity he kept his desires far from him.
Through thinness he made his color greenish by the great fortitude of his labor. For the emerald stones vary in color. Those that are found toward the side of the sunrise,
their green is very dark, and those found to the west of it are darker still.
And the one that comes out of the river Pishon displays its green mingled with light.

Like the true emerald, so too the high priesthood, each one individually, would show by the appearance of his face the deeds and labors of their courage, and with good order they held the word of teaching, instructing the people.
And if it appeared in a darkened color, it signified the color of his sins and the wickedness of his teaching.
And if it appeared white in color, it signified good deeds and better and pure teaching.
For thus says the prophet: "Comfort, comfort my people; priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem."
And again he says: "Go up on a high place, you who bring good news to Zion, and lift up your voice," and "tell my people their sin."
And no other, one successor after another, is able by any other means, nor by his own power, to know such teaching,
unless someone desires that precious stone, which is the Lord of life himself, and by its brilliance, as by the light of a mirror,
has his face enlightened, and by knowledge his mind, through truth and sincere faith, and as John, seeing face to face, says:
"This is the Lamb of God, who will wipe away the sins of the world." This is truly the precious stone, which is the diadem and lordly crown of his bride, the Church.
This stone is the emerald that was set on the shoulders of the high priest.
And on that emerald stone were inscribed the stones of the twelve tribes of Israel.
For truly through the high priests that precious stone, Christ, is made known, and the priests have received him and hold him, and through transmission by all, the knowledge of the Godhead.
And on this precious stone all the tribes are inscribed and are justified by that holy illumination, and they enter the holy church, and they spread out and give to each one grace,
to whom the keeping of holy virginity has been granted.
Some are vigilant and joyful, and some patient with courage, and some strengthened and understanding, and some with holy maidenhood.
All this the priesthood inscribes on that holy precious stone, which is the renewal by birth from above through the bath and through that holy illumination.
It presents the good hope through communion in the great counsel of God, and through the body and blood of Christ one becomes a companion and a child of God and a fellow heir with Christ,
to whom may there be attainment and rejoicing in that kingdom of the Son of God.
4. The jacinth stone. The fourth stone is the jacinth. And this is the first in the second row, on which the name of Judah is written thus.
Truly it clearly shows us the arrangement of the figure, the fourth position and the rulership.
And with all knowledge, by its setting, it arranges that square and rational tablet.
And he set it, polished, after that arrangement, for Judah was ruler over the people.
When they divided the people into four parts, Judah was commander and was encamped on the side of the sunrise,
but in order of succession he was the fourth of his brothers, and he was ruler and prospered in his kingship and leadership.
And the color of that stone shines like a burning coal, for from his tribe shone forth the one whom Isaiah, by the Holy Spirit, shows us, saying thus:
"I will turn your stones into a burning coal, and I will set up your foundations of sapphire stone" — which foreshadows to us two forms of kingship,
which the Lord showed us by his bodily appearance, through the likeness of the color of the two stones. For the sapphire stone resembles the color of purple.
It is manifest that Christ is the foundation and the beginning and the confirmation, the base of all things, and further the faith, unshakable and unchangeable.
For the jacinth stone is altogether the color of blood and the color of a burning coal.
It is the color of blood in that by the blood of the only-begotten Son of God all nations were redeemed, and the color of fire and of a burning coal in that
our Lord Jesus Christ will judge the living and the dead at his coming in glory.
And further, it is the name of the great and terrible mystery, which is the color of fire and of a burning coal, which the seraph took from that terrible altar,
where the Lord was and the six-winged seraphim stood before him with great and terrible reverence and service:
"The seraph had a burning coal in tongs," which is the mystery from that terrible altar, and he touched it to the mouth of the prophet.
He foreshadowed to all of us the great and terrible mystery, by its being received as a ransom for ourselves.
This is the purification of the prophet's lips, for this great and terrible mystery is itself the Lord's body and blood;
it is divided and granted to all of us; to those who act rightly in faith and deeds and to true believers it is given and granted for benefit and holiness.
But the foul and defiled, who approach with evil deeds, that is, the unbelievers, receive that royal mystery for wrath and judgment upon themselves,
for they became hasty and received the Lord's body and blood unworthily, as Paul the apostle says:
"Whoever eats and drinks the body and blood of the Lord unworthily eats and drinks to his own condemnation."
All this the jacinth stone foreshadows to us: redemption and wrath, redemption and holiness for the worthy, wrath and torment for the unworthy and the despisers.
This is the precious stone, namely the jacinth, on which was written the name of Judah, from whose tribe the Lord shone forth to us, and the foundations of Zion were laid,
the beginning and the foundation and "the head of the corner — the stone which the builders despised," who are the high priests,
who were trained and taught in the Law. They despised the Lord of the Law and put him away from themselves.
Those who were evildoers were disgraced and cast out of the priesthood and removed from it.
But the Lord of life, who is the precious stone, became the head of the corner, he who is himself the beginning and the end.
And he holds the confirmation of both, that is, of the old and of the new, as John says in his Revelation: "I am the beginning and I am the end."
And for the sake of his humbling he came down from heaven to earth, and as for the end, he ascended above the heavens and sat at the right hand of God on high.
And he is truly the beginning and the confirmation, for no one is able to build or to dismantle apart from that foundation, as Paul the apostle says:
"No one can lay any other foundation except this very one, which is Jesus Christ," and he is the head of the corner,
who holds both sides, which are the believers from the circumcision and from the uncircumcision.
And they came into one unity of life, and all became the temple of God.
This is the precious stone jacinth. It was found in the river Pishon, for Pishon is translated "mouth of fire."
Truly our Lord Jesus Christ spread the fire of fervor over the world, and he burned up the inflamed sins of all and purified all his saints.
For our Lord Jesus Christ breathed the Spirit upon his disciples and said to them: "Receive the Holy Spirit."
Of this the prophet Nahum also spoke: "Pishon came forth and spread over your face," for our Lord Jesus Christ rose from the dead; this he fulfilled and portrayed.
And the appearance of that stone is marvelous and precious and light-giving, and it is a shining coal the color of blood, and it sends forth radiance,
like kindled lamps, and no one is able to remove from it or to hide the lights of its radiance.
Truly, in this way all the saints who were made worthy to receive the Holy Spirit from Christ are illumined and glorious.
And now those who truly believe in our Lord Jesus Christ, the souls of all of them, being illumined, are glorified by him.
And through their humility the form of their angel-like conduct and of their thoughts is manifestly spread abroad, just as the face of the meek Moses became airy, and,
as from the sun, radiance shone forth from him, so that because of that glory of illumination no one could look at the face of Moses.
Likewise, further, the holy spirit of Elijah rested upon Elisha, "and the sons of the prophets saw him," and although he told no one,
they all cried out and said: "Behold, the spirit of Elijah has come to rest upon Elisha."
But truly the face of Stephen appeared illumined beyond radiance, and, illumined like an angel in appearance, the Spirit of grace appeared all the more to be resting upon him.
Although the impious high priests of the Jews were about to crush him with stones, he was not afraid,
but filled with that Spirit of grace and strengthened, he spoke before all of the opening of the heavens and of the sitting of the Son of God at the right hand of God.
And thus, by the confession of martyrdom and with great joy, he was crowned and martyred.
Such were all the saints: although they humbled themselves and lived afflicted and sorrowful in this world,
the light of the graces of the Holy Spirit manifestly shone forth from them, and they appeared glorious before God and men.
And that stone jacinth is found in the places that are called Severtida,
which is near the Libyans and Mauretania, Byzacena and Numidia, in the direction of Africa.
It was indeed fitting for this one of great understanding, whom the stone jacinth resembled,
to be found in those places of the Libyans near the sunrise, in the places of Ethiopia, which extend toward the south.
These are the blackened Ethiopians, who attained the graces of the Holy Spirit and, through great understanding, were brought near to that heavenly thought,
for the light of the power of Christ shone forth upon them and drove away the mist of the power of darkness, and he enlightened those who had been darkened by human deeds of wickedness
and of dark thought. And he purified the mind and made it shine and made it his friend.
And at his coming he revealed to all the thought of his divinity.
And by his love for humankind he dispelled the mist of the thought of the enemy.
And he planted in their thought the mind of Christ, in which Paul boasts when he says: "We have the mind of Christ."
And do not marvel at this, for the hyacinth stone is found at night, for it says thus in the Scriptures: "In the darkness a light has shone forth."
Truly the light of godliness has shone forth upon our darkened hearts and has removed from us the darkness of black and wicked deeds.
And by hidden thought, like the appearance of the hyacinth stone, he would reveal himself to his saints.
For formerly, among those who lived under the Law and the prophets, while the graces of the Gospel were not yet made manifest and spread abroad, many of the righteous sought Christ the Savior.
And he was revealed to them by hidden thought, and through their own knowledge they also prophesied to others.
For prophecies were made manifest concerning that stone and precious gem, Christ, as David says:
"His foundations are on the holy mountains," which means this: that his word came to all the prophets, and they bore witness to and preached the establishing of that foundation,
which the heavenly King came and established; and he brought that royal honor, setting it upon his people, and he made many worthy of the great honor of the priesthood.
And he set a crown upon his Church and made her queen and seated her at his right hand. And he imprinted in the middle of our foreheads that precious sign and adorned us.
For truly by that sign, by the cross of Christ and by his death, he has graciously given us life and the forgiveness of sins and has made us worthy of the glory and the dwelling place of the kingdom.
5. The sapphire stone. The fifth stone is the sapphire. On this was written the name of Dan, who came next by birth, inscribed on the oracle-plate near Judah.
For of the tribe of Dan many became judges of Israel, and afterward they came to be among the purple-clad magnates, for from this tribe was Eliab,
for he had charge of the tent of witness, for he worked the purple and managed all the service of the tent of witness.
And the lot of peace [?] fell to the tribe of Dan at the outflows of the Jordan.

The heavenly King purified the waters of the Jordan and made them the adornment and garment of the Church, dyed with his blood and purified by his divinity, and he made them into a purple garment and a royal adornment.
And all the peoples became clothed in Christ in the holy catholic Church, and they were crowned with a diadem of divine honor, and with knowledge they confessed the faith of the truth.
All this the sapphire stone foreshadowed to us. And through the name of the tribes it shows us, by intimation, its authority and royal service,
which prepared and administered the service of the tent of witness.
For from this tribe arose judges, who held the functions and standing of kings over the people.
And when the sapphire stone is ground down, its color changes to another color.
It intimates to us that from that tribe there are to be some who are good and some who are evil,
as some relate to us, adducing testimony from the Scriptures, that from this tribe the Antichrist will arise, who is the adversary of Christ.
For it says thus: "Dan: like a snake lying in wait on the roads, to strike the horse's heels and make its rider fall backward."
And they say that he who spoke thus was a prophet, and that he spoke of that fearful-looking figure in a parable, and he says thus:
"The salvation of the Lord": this figure indicates to us that if God had not given help at that time, no one would have been saved from his hands.
And again Moses says of him in his blessings: "He will begin with a leap, like a lion, from Bashan."
And further, it is to be understood by all that, just as John, in his enumeration of the thousands of the twelve tribes of Israel,
the holy prophets, who stood near the bride in the kingdom of heaven, did not count any from the tribe of Dan.
Was it that there were no virgins or saints in that tribe? There were many.
But I think that he intimates this figure because the adversary is to appear from that tribe.
He expelled Dan from the portion and in his place put Manasseh into the number.
And let your honor not be at all astonished that the same words of Scripture are said with reference to good or to evil things,
for we see the same words and figures adduced in the Scriptures in many ways.
For Christ is called a lion, yet not on account of the likeness of being of a lion's mind, and of eating blood, and of that brutish beastliness,
but Christ is called a lion because of his kingship, and for his distributing joy to all, and for his gathering many under his shade.
The devil too is called a lion, not because of kingship or for distributing joy to all, but because of his rapacity and his wicked tyranny.
Christ is further called a lion's whelp, for when the lion gives birth to the whelp, it lies dead for three days, and on the third day it rises,
just as Christ remained three days in the heart of the earth, crushed the gates of hell, and rose on the third day.
The devil too is called a lion and the whelp of a lion, for his rapacity and bestiality. And further, because of his sheep-like character, Christ is called a sheep.
His disciples too are called sheep, because of their quietness and gentleness and the fortitude of their deeds, who became bearers of fruit, like sheep.
Sinners too are called sheep. It says in the book: "Sheep were given over to Hell, and death shall shepherd them."
The Holy Spirit came down in the likeness of a dove at the streams of the Jordan.
It is because of the purity, quietness, and innocence of the dove. Ephraim too is called a senseless dove, for it is a brute creature and without endurance, and it dwells with those who harm it.
And so in all cases we find the same comparison applied sometimes to evil people and sometimes to good; to some the nature is likened, and to others the figure.
So also in the case of Dan we see the sapphire stone, where in one place good is foretold for that tribe and in another evil, for gold too,
which is marvelous to all and which comes out of the earth in the mountain: the Tempter showed all wealth in order to tempt.
And he intended to deceive the Lord of all creation, and he says:
"All the kingdom and glory of the earth has been given to me, and I will give it to you," and the rest that follows in order.
But the sapphire stone is without passing away, and it is a figure of good deliverance,
for many judges arose from the tribe of Dan and delivered Israel. As the ground powder of the stone, when mixed with milk, heals swellings and fleshy growths,
so those who select from the prophets teaching and knowledge concerning the age, and mix them, as with milk,
with the graces of Paul's preaching and the deeds of the miracles of the Gospel, [have?] minds pure, healed, and made blessed.
With a pure heart they saw God and became seers of God. The Israelites on the mountain saw God, and under his feet was sapphire.
For the foundation of Zion is this holy Church, which has become a queen, set as a crown and adorned with ornaments.
For thus it is written: "I will set your stones as of jacinth, and I will raise up your foundations as of sapphire."
For here too jacinth and sapphire come one after the other, for Judah signifies to us the kingship, and Dan the judgeship.
6. The jasper stone. The sixth stone is jasper, on which was written the name of Naphtali, who comes next by birth, for the name Naphtali is translated "widening."
For this stone has many kinds, and it is found not in one place but in many places, as we showed you above when we spoke about the stones.

And Naphtali is the one who was to inherit the broad expanse of the land and who distributed abundance to all Israel, for he was a worker and produced the fruit of abundance for the nourishment of all.
And Moses says concerning Naphtali: "You shall inherit the sea and the dry land," and then Isaiah the prophet says:
"The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, beyond the sea. The people who dwelt in darkness saw a great light.
And those who sat in darkness and the shadows of death, light shone upon them," and what it says next in order.
For in this place belonging to both tribes the Lord blessed bread, and with the five loaves he fed five thousand, and with the remainder
of the fragments they filled twelve baskets; and then with the seven loaves he satisfied four thousand, and with the remainder they filled seven hampers.
Indeed it was among these tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali that the Lord spoke the Beatitudes.
And seated on the mountain he continued that teaching with blessing, and he walked upon the waters of the sea, and having arrived at Capernaum, Peter's mother-in-law
he healed, and on the Sea of Gennesaret he performed miracles of a divine kind, and from those places and villages he brought forth those lights of the world,
who are these holy apostles, so that their radiance might appear to all the ends of the heavens.
The jasper stone, on which the name of Naphtali was written, and its appearance is like the color of emerald.
And again its color is like the sea: like the sea, it gives off a greenness of color from its gleams.
And in its greenness it is like the verdigris of copper, for Naphtali's inheritance fell to him near the Sea of Tiberias.
And it is near Zebulun and extends as far as the Great Sea. And jasper stones are of various kinds, and their color is of different sorts,
as we said earlier about all of it; and some are found near the Warm Water, and some are found in Amasia.
So also the miracles of God, for those apostles were chosen from many places:
some from those places of Naphtali; in Chorazin and Bethsaida and Capernaum and Magdala miracles of divine wonders were performed.
And from all places they gathered and followed the Lord, and were made worthy of blessing and healing, and they glorified the God of Israel.
And after a long time some turned away to godlessness, as Simon the sorcerer received baptism from Peter and became a preacher of falsehood and not of truth.
And Nicholas, one of those seven deacons, who was with Stephen, became a heretic of wickedness and led many astray.
And then Cerinthus and many others, who associated with Peter,
afterward turned away and became teachers of wickedness and not of good. As we said earlier about that stone, as though some revelation, as of a vision in dreams, were to occur [?].
And it is found in those places of Phrygia, as though in some kind of nest resembling earthenware, and there is a likeness and interpretation of its figure,
for in the extent of the teaching some confess that royal teaching of the Lord, and then fall into one teaching of falsehood after another,
for in the extent and depth and height of this teaching some go astray through negligence, some through evil deeds, and some through pride.
Their minds were carried away by ignorance, and in many places they said something different and swallowed down [?] all the more;
for the pagans were near, and out of ignorance [?], who were accustomed to the manner of ravening wolves, together with the eating of blood, and were likened in their habits to evil beasts.
Just as that stone has an appearance of blood color mixed, as if with milk, so too the wicked pagans are joyful in the good work of God [?] and do not know the true God,
but always in their own wickedness they live and die.
But the holy preachers, the true apostles, who were made worthy to receive those powers of Christ, nourish the whole world, as if with milk, with that divine apostolic teaching.
With the blood of Christ they wiped away the sins of the believers, and with the Gospel, by the word of the Lord, they drove out the forms of beastliness from the thoughts of many.
These apostles were chosen from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun, and they were filled with the Spirit of power.
And it says: From him, from God the Christ, they received very great gifts, and they spread them without payment to all the ends of the earth; they drove out demons and cut apart the bonds of sins.
And they adorned [?] unbelief, and taught all the gentiles the faith of truth.
And all of them, filled with good works, glorified the one God.
7. The ligure stone. The seventh stone, the ligure, set and placed on the rational plate.
And this is the first in the third row, set and placed in sequence according to his birth, and the name of Gad is written on that stone.
And the lot of inheritance fell to Gad near Reuben, beyond the river Jordan, and between Gad and Reuben is the half-tribe of Manasseh.
And that portion of Gad reaches toward the north, and it goes and extends as far as the border of Dan and of the inheritance of Reuben,
from the ravine of Arnon as far as the city of Aroer, and his inheritance reaches as far as Asura, and to Madaba and Brea.
And as far as the border of Mount Nebo, and it reaches as far as Heshbon and Elealeh and as far as Jazer.
And in the midst of these and between them is the half-tribe of Manasseh.
And it stretches as far as Bethron, as far as the Jordan, and reaches as far as the head of the mountain, as far as Bashan.
And from there it reaches as far as Gaza, and it borders Reuben and Gad. But the ligure stone, as we said before, is obscure and hard to find.
But the account has come down to us from those of former times, and we spoke of it before at some length.
I think, then, that this is the jacinth that is mentioned in the divine books.
And the appearance of that ligure is honey-colored and purple-colored. The stone has one name but many colors, like the jacinth.
And on it was written the wonderful name of Gad, who is near the half-tribe of Manasseh.
I think that "the Tishbite" is by nature to be understood as one who is in Gilead, which is the dwelling place between the half-tribe of Manasseh and Gad.
Coming from there, Elijah the prophet arrived, the son of Ahimah, who was of the kin of Aaron and lived in these places and dwellings on account of the priesthood of that tribe,
who were scattered among all the tribes of Israel, as Jacob says:
"I will divide you in Jacob and scatter you in Israel," for because of the priesthood and their being Levites they settled here and there in all those places.
But the tribe of Simeon, through learning from the books and through the wisdom of knowledge, and for the teaching of all, settled among the other tribes as well.
Now do not be surprised that we have mentioned Elijah the prophet together with Gad and have brought forward the figure of that stone in connection with him,
for he was by nature of the seed of Gilead, near the tribe of Joseph and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
But in many places we find priests and high priests who came each from their own tribes.
We find the high priest Abiathar in the city of Nob, which was a city set apart for the priests from the inheritance of the tribe of Judah.
And Samuel was settled in the tribe of Ephraim, being an Ephrathite. And Eli dwelt in Shiloh, which was the inheritance of Benjamin.
And thus the priestly families settled, dispersed and scattered throughout all the tribe.
I think that the ligure stone is the jacinth, whose power we wished to show.
But as for the ligure stone, as we said before, it has not become clear where it is found.
Next I will begin to inquire further into it, and out of love of the truth I will say:
If it is brought near fire, it quenches the fire's power, just as Elijah ascended in the chariot of fire and suffered no harm.
And he called down fire from above, and it came upon the companies of fifty and the captains of fifty, and then, through the offerings, by [?] descending against the priests of Baal.
And he himself suffered no harm within that mighty fire, but remained uninjured.
It seems to me that the three youths who were in Babylon and suffered no harm from the fire were of this world.
Truly wondrous is the power of that stone, for all the saints were portrayed in it.
For the three youths were cast into the fire and suffered no harm at all. Rather, they persuaded the king and brought all the unbelievers to the knowledge of God.
And idol-worship was brought into contempt by them, and they crushed the idols that would otherwise have led them astray, as was being done in other places, from nation to nation.
And they turned people from unbelief to the faith of the truth.
Just as this jacinth stone, which is in the depth of the abysses and which no one is able to bring up,
except by the flesh of a lamb and the rushing descent of an eagle, so also is holy boldness.
I speak of Elijah, and of the three youths who were in Babylon, and of the blessed Thecla, who showed courage in the times of her trial.
And if it was not their own power, what brought about their deliverance?
It was the coming of the Lamb who blotted out the sins of the world, and who, like an eagle, by the might of the Godhead, was exalted and ascended above the heavens.
For this is what the account of that precious stone shows us. I speak of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego under the power of death.
Moses says that until the coming of Christ, as we find, all souls were under the power of death:
as the apostle Paul says: "As long as Moses is read, that same veil clings to the old law."
And when the grace of the new law, Christ, arrived, that veil was taken away, and from then on immortality was revealed.
If that law which brought death was attended by glory, how much more will this law of life be attended by glory?
All this we have said to show that the power of death is spoken of as lasting until the coming of Christ.
And although it is said: from Adam until the coming of Christ there are many.
For this reason there is also something else to be stated and interpreted. But was it the law that condemned? Far from it!
Nor was that writing a killer; rather, it was deadly to those who committed transgression and sin. And it is not that the law was meant for condemnation. Far from it!
Rather, those who did not keep righteousness and purity brought upon themselves the judgment of death, through negligence and those evil deeds.

And the glory was not on account of the law because it was laid down by God, but because the face of that glorious Moses was glorified; yet the detention of death, burial and corruption belonged to that glorious body of his.
This is the undoing of those glories. You said that the body of our Savior was buried,
but his body did not see corruption, nor was his soul detained in hell, for on the third day he rose.
For he says thus: "I will rise with my glory," as the prophet says:
"Awake, O my glory, with psalm and harp," just as the disciples said in this New [Testament]:
"Awake, Lord, for we are perishing in this tossing of the sea." And the Lord awoke from sleep.
I speak of the sleep of his body, and of his rebuking, by his glory, the sea and its tossing, with fear and with that lordly word.
And the sea was silenced and stilled. And the prophets foretold concerning the sufferings and the resurrection from the dead.
And concerning the awakening it says thus: And I will awaken
at dawn, and I will awake with my glory. And that awakening belongs to the nature of the body, and what it says, "with my glory," is the nature of the Godhead.
Now, because of the weightiness of this matter, let us extend this discourse and bring forward what it says,
that it is not so only until Moses, but that the books speak of that power of death until the coming of Christ.
And further it is written in the law of the Lord that iniquities came forth in Babylon from the elders who judged the people.

And when the five books of Genesis have been read through, and Joshua son of Nun, and Judges, and Ruth, and the books of Kings, and Chronicles, and the select writings, which are in verse, and the books of the prophets,
we still do not find these words of the law of the Lord stated, to which Daniel testified and which he spoke.
And when the books of Jeremiah are searched, in which he says thus: He assigned to the people seventy years of being in that captivity.
And he said to the sons of Israel: "In the land of the Babylonians take wives for yourselves and have children, and plant vineyards and eat of their fruit."
And after this he says: Let them take up this proverb in the land of the Babylonians and say this: What may the Lord do to you?
And may he lay you to sleep, as he did Ahab and Zedekiah, whom the king of the Babylonians roasted [?] on a griddle for lawlessness and adultery,
who fornicated with the wives of their fellow citizens and spoke a lying word in my name, which I had not commanded.
And I am witness of all this, says the Lord Almighty.
Truly he says this concerning the leaders, for one of the leaders was Zedekiah and the other was Ahab.
For Daniel does not state their names, but he shows them to us in other books,
in which the revelations of Daniel are found, for there he gives their names in writing: the name of the one was Aba, and of the other, Ada.
But Jeremiah speaks of the punishment of those lawless judges and elders in a different way, saying that Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, roasted them on a griddle.
But Daniel says this: "All the people rose up against Susanna to stone her."
We also find another revelation of Daniel, that a rod of fire fell down from heaven between the two elders, and it did not burn them up at once, but repaid them with torment for a long time.
And now, concerning the punishments that came upon those wicked judges, the elders, I will show you that what Jeremiah and Daniel said is not in conflict.
All this punishment came and reached those godless elders who transgressed the law, for the law commanded not to accept a bribe and not to pervert justice,
and not even to pity a poor man in judgment, nor to show partiality to a rich man, but to follow equal justice.
But they sold justice for bribes. And in that knowledge concerning lawfulness [?], their nesting thoughts gave birth to that wicked lust.
And they grew eager against the holy Susanna.
And vengeance from God revealed it to the youth Daniel, and by a just judgment he destroyed [?] those lawless judges before everyone.
And by that judgment Daniel commanded, in accordance with the law, that those lawless judges be stoned.
And one [?] came out to stone those lawless elders. The just judgment given by Daniel was revealed by God to all.
He gave over to his own judgment [?]; he sent down from heaven, in witness of that true judgment, so that all, being terrified [?]:
Let no one be eager to pervert justice for a bribe or to show partiality in judgment. And there was great fear because of that judgment, in this way.
When the people began to stone those wicked elders, their souls had not yet departed from their wicked bodies, when a terrible sight appeared [?]:
"A rod of fire fell down among them and burned up those wicked elders.
And while the embittered souls of those unseemly elders had not yet departed, all were terrified, and they spread the news here and there and in Babylon.
And the terror of that judgment reached the ears of King Nebuchadnezzar.
He was amazed and stunned at the justice [?] ... and if you do not take it upon yourselves, God will condemn you for the grief of this people.
And in this way they would persuade the women. And those women gave themselves over to the filth of fornication with those elders.
And Daniel testifies to this account, for he says: "Thus you used to do to the daughters of Israel.
And they, in dread and fear, gave themselves to you in filth. But this daughter of Judah did not take part in your lawless deeds."
The prophecy of Jeremiah also testifies to this and says: "Blows shall come upon those leaders because of their lawlessness.
"and they committed fornication with the women, their fellow citizens, and prophesied a word of falsehood to them in the name of the Lord, and I, the Lord, had not commanded them."
And they themselves bore witness, as witnesses, to my words, for this is the account concerning them.
In the name of the Lord they seduced those women and said to them: "The Christ is to come forth from your kin."
And they spoke to her with the word of the Lord, and the Lord had not spoken to them.

For this reason the Lord sent upon those elders of lawlessness the punishment of fire by that rod, and burning by that griddle, through the wrath of Nebuchadnezzar and the conviction brought by the prophet Daniel.
But I have given this whole account for the sake of the correspondence with that precious stone, and for the sake of the word of the apostle, who says:
"Death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned."
For this reason Daniel says, as it is written in the law of the Lord: "Lawlessness came forth from those elders."
Do you see that Daniel too calls Jeremiah's words the law? And the Lord says in the Gospel: "The law and the prophets were until John."
Do you see that the dominion of death lasted until Christ? And all the souls of the saints, and those who had not sinned,
stood confined under the slavery and dominion of death, until the Lamb of God was slain, who blotted out the sins of the world.
Together with the soul, the divine Word descended to Hades, while the Lord's flesh on the wood was being burned like that of a lamb.
And those raging torrents cast him down, and they laid him in the tomb hewn in the rock.
Although soul and body had separated from one another, the Word of God did not separate from his soul and his body.
Just as there the flesh of the lamb, joined to the precious stone, was brought up by the swooping down of the eagles, so too it came to pass in the slaying and passion of Christ:
in the descent of the Lord's flesh into the tomb and the descent of the souls into Hades.
Those precious stones, the righteous, having adhered to that Lamb who descended to them, "were lifted up and came up from there."
Truly, through the great likeness of the finding of this stone, this explanation has shown us gain and profit.
For by that descent into Hades the Lord brought the righteous souls up from Hades, crushed the gates of death, and took out all of them from its midst;
the Lord drew up and brought up his servants, the meek and quiet. And he himself testifies to this and says: "When I am lifted up, I will draw them to myself."
This was accomplished not only on the cross, but also in the holy resurrection, which took place on the third day.
Other writings also testify to this, that his soul was not left in Hades, this very soul that had descended to Hades together with the Godhead.
He broke the bolts and cut the bonds of Hades, and delivered all his saints by his own power.
And when that valiant shepherd rose from the dead, "he breathed on his disciples and said to them: 'Receive the Holy Spirit.'"
And then the Lord of all was exalted to heaven, with the flesh, in fullness, just as he had become man in flesh and soul, and he accomplished everything,
He truly rose and made the flesh incorruptible and immortal, and the soul, joined together with the flesh, into oneness with the nature of the Godhead.
With great glory he was exalted to heaven and sat at the right hand of the Father. And he ascended above the heavens in that only-begotten flesh.
The hope of the resurrection and of the kingdom was announced as good news to all the saints. Truly wonderful is the parable and the interpretation of that precious stone.
Although the ligure is that jacinth stone, its power has shown us all of this.
Now as to how it came to be named ligure, which means "tail of a cow", the cow has the color of this stone. And that animal was called by the name ligure.
For in the land of the Egyptians there are wild cows, which are called babalon.
And the tip of the tail of that babalon gives off a brilliance of green color, like that stone.
And because of the likeness of color they gave this name to that stone.
And if anyone gives a drink from that stone, and if anyone gives women its run-off liquid to drink, conception comes about and easy childbirth.
The name of Gad was rightly inscribed on this stone, for Leah gave Zilpah in her own place, and those who came forth from her by Jacob Leah raised as her own children.
Zilpah was reckoned in place of Jacob, and all of them became precious stones and were made worthy to be called a holy race. And just as people drink of that ligure stone for easy childbirth,
so too the prophets and apostles and all the righteous became precious blood. And they received grace from God.
They bestowed every good thing upon people, just as Elijah gave back to the widow the one raised from the dead, and Elisha by his prayer granted childbearing to the Shunammite woman.
And the waters of Jericho, which were barren, became blessed and fruitful through the prayer of Elisha.
So too were those holy ranks of the apostles, for the churches and peoples of the gentiles, who bore children with difficulty.
The disciples received power from Christ, went out, and preached the gospel in all places.
And through the preaching of the gospel, given by grace, they turned to birth by faith and to kinship with the one born of God, and by that preaching they proclaimed the gospel to all.
Rejoice, you church that does not bear children!
Rouse yourself and cry out, you who have not been in labor, for the children of the one made desolate are more numerous than those of the one who has children.
The apostles performed many signs among all the gentiles and did away with those who practiced deception before people's eyes.
They drove the demons out from them and from their lands, and they crushed and scattered all the idols and wiped out idol-worship from among them.
Receive with kindness these things that have been said, and the benefit that we may gain from the power of that ligure stone.
And let no one say, as though you were saying: "Nowhere do we find that ligure stone, nor where it comes from, nor where it is to be found."
Speak of all this by way of comparison. Many kinds of stones are mentioned, and no one recognizes those stones.
But from the account of the old books, through understanding, their color is known and the benefit to be had from them can be understood.
And there are many stones which first bore another name, and afterward it was changed to a different one.
But now the stone ligurion had its own name from the ancients themselves, and afterward it bore another name, by which I suppose it is called jacinth in the books.
All this is the knowledge of this precious stone, and what we have said are the powers of its interpretation.
8. The stone agate. The eighth stone is the agate, which is second in its order, in the third appointed row of the tablet.
And the name of Asher was fittingly written upon it. And he comes next by birth among the sons of Israel.
And the name of Asher is translated 'wealth.' And in the blessings of his sons he speaks of him in due order:
"Asher, you were in fullness and in the richness of wheat, and from you all the rulers of Israel were nourished."
For the places of his dwelling were fruitful and abundant.
And he worked at his abundance and gave the region a great quantity of fruitfulness. And he was able to nourish the kings and rulers of that land.
As we said before, one by one, concerning the character of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel,
the tribe of Asher was skilled in the work and labor of the land, and they satisfied the need of all.
And the color of this stone itself, which is the agate, is lion-colored. That stone is not purple, nor green-colored, but earth-colored and reddish.
It is rich and not sandy. This is earth that is sinewy and strong and brings forth much fruitfulness.
And it does not destroy the seed, and it is productive in many places. And it fills kings and their peoples with richness.
Truly well engraved is the inscription of that stone, which took and held the name of Asher, the appearance of that stone's color being lion-colored, for it is called royal.
And know that in one place it likens him to a serpent lying in ambush, and in another place it says that he will begin to leap [?] like a lion.
For thus Moses says concerning him: "Dan will begin to leap [?] like a lion from Bashan."
Truly it is a marvel that the color of that stone resembles the color of the lion,
for he was called a lion in likeness to his strength and to the might of his dominion and to the wrath of his heart against all.
So too all the power of the wealth of that Asher, through which there were provisions and foods,
the riches and powers of kings and of all the [?] of high priests and priests, and the sustenance and wealth of the temple of the Lord,
all were nourished by the labor and fruitfulness of Asher. And the color of that stone is like the color of the lion.

It signified the change of the law, which appeared in the preaching of the Gospel through the bestowal of grace by the hands of the apostles, on account of which David in the Psalms calls the apostles sons of God.
For he spoke thus: "Offer to the Lord, sons of God," and then he says: "Offer to the Lord the young of rams," tribes and peoples, and then he says:
"He shall live, and there shall be given to him of the gold of Arabia," which was manifested at the resurrection of the Lord, when he took upon himself the passion and rose.
And to him was given that tested gold, which he refined and purified and made into the ornament of his own kingdom.
This first became an enlightener in the region of Arabia and attained, through submission, to the kingdom of God, and concerning this it says, "The kings of Arabia shall bring him gifts."
Some of this was fulfilled by those Magi who came and brought gifts and worshiped the Lord, and some was fulfilled by the hand of the eunuch of Queen Candace,

and then still more by the hand of Paul the apostle, "who went to Damascus and first came to the region of Arabia," and preached there for just three years and enlightened them with the word of the Gospel.
After three years he went up to Jerusalem, so that the apostle who walks with the Bridegroom might bring the faith of the Arabians and the Sabaeans as a gift,
for according to that Law he was called a bridegroom, whose name was written on the stone that was the ornament of the priest, for this is Asher.
The wealth of that king is a beautiful sight, which is the agate stone.
Let us also speak about this from the New Law, for it is written there in those praises of Asher. And it says: "The wealth of the Gentiles shall be transferred to you."
Truly the Gentiles have been transferred to such a holy hope in God, and have received the strength of lions and the wealth of Asher, they who once were assailants and had grown strong in rebellion.
And through disobedience they had put the fear of the Lord far from themselves, and in their folly they were hastening along under the power of the devil.
