But when they turned back, they submitted to that command of God and entered the house of the Lord, which is this [?] of rebellion.
And out of the strength of paganism they displayed the strength that they had; they came out of folly and increased in wisdom in the might of faith,
and by the grace of that heavenly King and by the nature of that virginal dignity, for by the power of the Holy Spirit it grew gloriously strong.
Do you see how many mighty things there are that have been revealed to us from the Old and New Laws through the testimony of this precious stone,
on which in the beginning the names of their tribes were written, and which was fulfilled as a parable for spiritual people?
It speaks further about the healing property of the stone, that when ground into powder it heals the venom of asps and vipers and scorpions.
So also God would look upon the sacrifices and prayer and supplication of those former righteous leaders and kings.
And by the might granted to them from him, they would crush and trample all the Gentile nations and assailants.
Let us bring forward further evidence from the New Law as well, when the apostles appointed ministers who nourished the poor and the widows and also offered their very selves as a sacrifice.
And because of their great zeal, the power of healings was given to them by the graces of God. For it says this:
"Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and to trample the power of the enemy, and nothing shall be able to harm you."
Truly that agate stone, on which the name of Asher was written, has great power,
for from it the account of the Old Laws was prefigured, and by that spiritual figure the Church of God was filled and made perfect.
9. The amethyst stone. The ninth stone: amethyst. And it was inscribed on the third row.
On the last [stone] was written the name of Issachar, who is next in order of birth.
And Jacob says this in the blessings: "Issachar, the heart has desired [?] what is good;
you shall rest among your portions and may you find rest, for it is good, and your land also, for it is rich.
He put his shoulders to the work and became a tiller of the land."
If that is so, the husbandry of Issachar was made manifest, like the color of the amethyst stone, when one looks at its shifting color:
its color flares up to the color of fire, and it is also seen as white in color, and also like wine that is the color of water.
Thus the appearance of its color is altogether varied. And further, there are many kinds of it, which are found in the mountains, in waterless places.
Its color is like that of the hyacinth stone, which is whitish. But the kind that is found in ravines is like the color of blood.
And the kind that is found near the seashore is just as very pure as that on the mountains.
And the kind that is found in snowy places is darkish. And this one is hard. This is what was said of Issachar concerning vine-dressing.
This stone is wonderful and beautiful to see. So too Issachar was watchful and quiet in his husbandry among Israel.
And he was never overcome by drunkenness, lest his sons should scorn him and inherit a curse.
And indeed they did not go forth in mockery [?] with the base revelries of those scribes and Pharisees, who were shaking their heads and saying:
"Ah, you are the one who destroys this temple and in three days raises it up!"
And the portion of Issachar's inheritance fell to him as a portion in the region of Galilee, near Mount Tabor,
which the Lord ascended, where Moses and Elijah were with him, and some of the other apostles.
And great divine visions took place there. This much has been said about the amethyst stone, on which the name of Issachar was written.
And there was given to him by blessing a portion of inheritance, for his labor, for husbandry.
Come, let us now see the spiritual grace of Christ in those blessings,
how he blessed the apostles and sent them out to work in all places, and the Holy Spirit was given from those graces of God, for Paul the apostle says thus:
"We are God's building, we are fellow workers with God," and there is to be no negligence or folly in us,
but rather always wisdom and watchfulness with courage, so that they may unceasingly accomplish spiritual labor in divine things.
10. The purple stone. The tenth stone is the purple. This is the head of the fourth row.
Some have called it beryl. But it is purple in color rather than beryl.
And on it was written the name of Zebulun, who comes next in the order of the sons of Jacob, and according to the way in which the portion of inheritance fell to him.
And his dwelling is near the sea, and the riches of the sea came to him from every side.
And he was ruler over all sailors, concerning which Jacob also says in the blessings:
"Zebulun shall dwell on the shore of the sea, and he shall manage his seafaring near Sidon."
Truly, the purple stone was inscribed in good and proper order, for all the wealth and gifts were offered from there to the temple of God,
for gold was brought from Tarshish by ships, for Solomon would send them, and they brought from even more distant places elephant tusks [?],
ostriches and [?] and also other precious stones, and stones whose color is like gold.
And they speak of this in many ways: some call it Carthage, and others say from Abioth [?] and Nabdea [?], from Attica and Aradia [?], and some say from Rhodes [?].
And the men of the Ionians say: from great Rome and Spain and from every region by sea they brought goods to one another for mutual profit.
For Zebulun was a partner and fellow helper to all of them.
There the purple stone was found, and it was called purple, for it gives off brilliance, is gold-colored, and is not destroyed by fire.
Near this inheritance is Nazareth of Galilee,
in which the good news of the birth and of Mary's conception was announced by Gabriel, and that heavenly gold was given from the holy virgin at Nazareth, where the conception took place.
To Nazareth was given the conception, and to Bethlehem the birth, from which came the beginning of the buildings.
And Bethlehem is translated "house of fruitfulness," where the birth of the Lord took place, and in Zion he laid his foundation, for the cross is called the foundation of the churches.
And he who was crucified became the Redeemer, the beginning of all believers, and he laid the first foundation upon the height of the cross.
And that precious stone was buried in the tomb in the places of Zion, and the building of salvation came about, and, risen from the dead, he completed that spiritual edifice,
for on the cross water and blood came forth from him, from that foundation itself, which serves to confirm the two parties. The water came for this reason,

because it became the washing of salvation from the dross of our sins, and the blood, by being sprinkled upon us, for justification and purification, by which we became partakers and fellow heirs of Christ.
And built upon that cornerstone foundation, he raised us to the height of heaven, for our Lord Jesus Christ became the cornerstone of the corners, and those built upon him are firm.
On both sides he completed the building of all the ends of heaven: with the circumcised and the uncircumcised.
In unity we were all built up spiritually through that Gospel of truth.
This is the purple stone, which is like light in appearance and beautiful, gold-colored.
And it is found in the pit called the Mouth of the Rock, in Achaemenid Babylon.
And let no one suppose that "Achaemenid" was given as a name for nothing, or ask what profit there was in adding its name to Babylon,
for we see this said many times in the books, and the giving of a name to teach in one and the same way, for it says thus:
Joshua son of Nun, and Joshua son of Jozadak, and Jesus son of Sirach, and Jesus our Lord:
By that addition of a name a distinction was made in the one kind; and no one speaks of or inquires about the one
who does not resemble that one kind but shows by himself his own character. For the name Abraham is spoken, and it declares him by itself.
And he is called Isaac, and his name needs no other name. So too Jacob is made known by himself alone. But for those who bear two names,
it is necessary, so that the one may show the natural [one], for sameness of name shows only itself.
Now Babylon is called Achaemenid, because there is also another Babylon, a fortress and tower near Egypt.
Now by the addition of the second name he teaches us which Babylon it is.
It is said that there was a certain man named Achaemenidon, who was the father of King Cyrus,
who renewed Babylon a second time and gave it a name after the name of his father: Achaemenid Babylon, in which that crimson stone is found.
And it serves as a remedy for those suffering in the stomach and those suffering in the belly, when someone drinks it ground up.
It is proper to state the names of all the places, so that you may know where that crimson stone comes from, or what kind it is.
Now let us consider Zebulun, whose name was inscribed on that crimson stone. Nazareth was part of the inheritance of Zebulun, where the conception of our Lord Jesus Christ was granted to the Virgin,
whom that crimson stone resembles, on which was inscribed the name of Zebulun, who had great wealth from the sea.
Truly, gifts from all the ends of the heavens are offered to our Lord Jesus Christ, who is himself the precious merchandise.
And he healed all wounds and pains, not only visible ones but invisible ones as well, which no human being is able to do.
But because he himself is the only-begotten Son of God, he performed very great mighty works and granted to those who believe in him the forgiveness of sins.
11. The beryl stone. The eleventh stone is the beryl, which appears darkish but gives off light; it is sea-colored and in appearance like jacinth.
It came about by that ordinance wonderfully: the name of Joseph was inscribed on it, for he was the eleventh among his brothers,
who was most wonderfully glorified among his brothers through that very striving of God on his behalf.
And he turned the curses of Reuben into blessing and turned his ruin into life,
for Reuben lost all the honor of his birthright, since the birthright and the priesthood and the kingship were rightly Reuben's.
And weakened by the incontinence of his desire, he was overcome by the lust of his flesh and defiled his father's bed, on account of which Jacob became a righteous judge.
And he judged those transgressions of Reuben and took from him the priesthood and the kingship.
He held the birthright established by birth, but he took from him the priesthood and the kingship.
And by an offering he presented Levi as chief, for the priesthood over the tribes.
And from then on he sought out and chose that good lineage for kingship. He signifies this by the daughter, from whose lineage Christ was to be born.
And in those blessings Jacob began with Judah and said: "Judah, your brothers shall praise you.
Your hands shall be on the shoulders of your enemies, and the sons of your father shall bow down to you. Judah is a lion's whelp."
Do you see that he gave him all royal authority and the honor of power, and cast his enemies down under his feet?
It was Levi and Judah who received the honor of the priesthood and of the royal diadem.
Levi held the priesthood over that lineage because he showed his zeal against the violence, from those kindreds of the woman [?],
for woman has been given as a stumbling block, and as a helper, and as a test of courage, so that one may conquer and win the crown through courage, because by a woman all perish.
And as the son of Sirach says: "By the hand of a woman we all die, and again by a woman we are all made alive."
Truly, that light of Christ shone forth from Mary.
He gave life to all who believe in him, for from many women they inherited shame, defilement and sin.
Because of a woman many showed courage and became crowned. Reuben was clothed in shame through a woman, and he lost the priesthood and the kingship.
Joseph trampled down the raging desire of his mistress, showed courage, and took possession of the kingship of the land of Egypt,
and he ruled over his brothers. Levi, in turn, took up zeal on account of the defilement of his sister, and he avenged the shame on those lawless Shechemites.
And his lineage attained to the high priesthood. Judah, in turn, conquered desires by repentance and endurance.
Although at one time he fell into rashness toward Tamar, his daughter-in-law, yet that too was a foreshadowing on account of the good design
which joined Tamar as rightful kin, she whom Matthew includes in the count in his Gospel. But Judah thought thus:
that Tamar had fallen through the incontinence of desire into fornication, and he ordered his daughter-in-law to be stoned.
But when he came to the matter itself, he said: "Tamar is more justified than I."
And from then on Judah no longer touched a woman, for nowhere do we find that after that affair with Tamar he had another wife.
And Tamar too touched no one after giving birth to that rightful lineage. And so by their endurance they displayed the deed of their courage.
And so Judah bridled that desire with vigilance and courage, and became worthy to attain to kingship and to the wondrous birth of Christ,
just as Matthew the Evangelist included him in the count and ordering of the generations. He writes: "From Abraham to David, fourteen generations,
and from David to the Babylonian captivity, fourteen generations, and from the Babylonian captivity to Christ, fourteen generations."

He openly listed only the names of the fathers, and of the mothers he nowhere included any in the count except four alone, and of these some were from among the Gentiles and some did not walk uprightly.
And nowhere does he mention the courageous women who, by the nature of that lineage, belonged to the count of the generations:
Neither Sarah, nor Rebekah, nor Leah, nor Rachel, who were the true first women.
And Judah begins, and he says: "Judah begot Zerah of Tamar," she who seemed contemptible to him.
He would magnify her, and it would be made manifest to all that he joined her name to the kindred, to the reckoning of Judah.
And he mentions not only Tamar, but other foreign women as well. And he joined them to the reckoning thus: "Perez begot Hezron.
Hezron begot Ram. Ram begot Amminadab. Amminadab begot Nahshon. Nahshon begot Salmon. Salmon begot Boaz of Rahab." And Rahab [?]

She is Rahab the harlot, and let no one suppose, because of the lengthening of this name, that she was some other person; for this is the very Rahab, Raab the harlot, since "Hebron" is said many times.
And it was also given the name Hebron. And there are many names that are changed in this way by addition. Boaz was from that harlot.
"Boaz begot Obed of Ruth." This woman was in no way close to the race of Israel, but she was an Ammonite.
Ammon was the second offspring of Lot by his daughter, for he was the second offspring joined to the reckoning of the kindred, from that wife of Lot from Sodom.
And all this that happened gives to all the consolation of waiting in hope, for whoever wishes to set out toward what is good meets no delay.
Likewise they run toward evil of their own will. For this reason, and by that writing, Saint Matthew the Evangelist joins them to the reckoning and says: "Boaz begot Obed of Ruth.
Obed begot Jesse. Jesse begot David. David begot Solomon of the wife of Uriah," who is Bathsheba herself.
For the affairs of Bathsheba had become entirely manifest, how they were, or how she was the wife of Uriah;
therefore he did not even mention her name, for it was manifest to all through the name of Uriah.
But the name of Ruth can in no way be explained, apart from the stating of that name, either from her husband, or else as it would have been said by those of earlier times.
Likewise Rahab's name, and in the same way Tamar's too. But he did not mention any of those more valiant women of earlier times,
who were renowned in Israel and married according to custom; rather, he mentioned those foreign women who did not marry lawfully.
Now all this is evident. Even though those who were not of the race of Abraham were also mentioned,
the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, likewise through that birth in the flesh, blotted out the sins of many, and they were joined to righteousness.
Not as if in sin, far from it! For those who commit sin, even if they were within, would still be far from Christ;
but those who have been removed from sins and drawn near to the works of righteousness are joined to the tribe and company of the righteous,
having become believers in that good hope of Christ, in that the only-begotten Son of God came and became man.
And he gathered those who were scattered through that birth from the one Virgin, who was from the two peoples: from the circumcision and from the uncircumcision.
By his mercy he saved those who had become far from the Law, for he himself was the head of the corner and also one,
for he established that wall as his own, and reconciled both to one another in himself, and joined them to righteousness,
So that none of those who were circumcised earlier may boast that the fruit of righteousness came forth from them.
Rather, let the Israelites who have believed in Christ know that the true rock, which was despised by the builders,
is a precious stone for all of us, for our Lord Jesus Christ came and joined both sides to himself: Rahab from the foreigners,
who put away her sins, and Solomon the Israelite from the tribe of Judah; and again Tamar from the Philistines, and Judah from the race of the blessed Abraham;
Ruth from the Ammonites and Sodomites, Boaz from Judah and the tribe [?]. And envy is venom and an evil beast.
"An evil beast has devoured him, and an evil beast has carried him off." Truly, excessive envy is an evil beast.
And then and there it was believed in the house of Jacob that his son was dead. But Joseph had been established as king in Egypt.
And it was not Joseph who was stained with blood, but his garment. So too Israel laid their hands on the Savior.
It was not possible to lay hands on the Godhead, for the nature of the Godhead is impassible, but the Lord's flesh gives forth blood.
Christ is impassible, and yet Christ also suffered. He suffered in the Lord's flesh.
It was not that the flesh had been separated from the nature of the Godhead; rather, it was inseparable from the nature of the Godhead, which had been united to the flesh.
But the nature of the Godhead did not suffer, yet it was willingly with the humanity, for the inseparable nature of each of them was Christ's suffering for us in the flesh.
For it was not that the suffering was removed from him, nor was the humanity separated from him, for the unity of the Son of God was without removal and without separation.
And in the joined unity of Godhead and humanity he is one Lord, one Christ.
"If they had known the Lord of glory, they would not have crucified him." This humanity too is called Lord of glory, through its unity with the Godhead.
And just as when a garment is soiled and dyed with blood, it is on the garment, yet the soiling with blood is not thought to belong to the garment,
but of that garment of Christ alone [?], by the blood on the garment his death is spoken of, the death of the one who wore that garment.
Although Joseph had not died, it was said of the body that wore the garment, and the staining with blood was attributed to that body, yet it was the garment that was stained with blood.
And the staining with blood is not thought to belong to the garment, but to the one who has put it on.
So too the sufferings cannot touch the Godhead, yet it has been united to the Godhead, so that our salvation may come from God.
And let our hope not be in a human being, but in God, for it is written:
"Cursed be the one who places hope in a human being," so that no one may say that the Godhead suffered.

He clothed himself with what belongs to suffering, and he who was impassible with respect to suffering, as though the sufferings were reckoned to the impassible one, did so in order that by what belongs to suffering he might do away with our suffering and death.
Thus also in the house of Israel the name of Christ is spoken to this very day. And Christ the King is Lord.
Just as the sons of Jacob had the garment of Joseph and told their father of Joseph's death, while Joseph was reigning over the Egyptians,
In this way the Jews had the body of the crucified one, like the garment of Joseph, and they carefully laid it in the tomb and carefully sealed the grave.
And they begged Pilate to order the soldiers to guard the grave carefully.
And just as the house of Jacob had the garment of Joseph while Joseph was reigning in Egypt, so also Christ, the King of all, descended into hell.
And he loosed the bonds of Adam, who had been bound by that evil tyrant.
Christ the great King both bound the tyrant and slew the tyranny of the devil, which is death, and plundered his house, which is the abysses of hell,
and he took as his own captives those who had been taken captive by death, and he delivered the souls of all from the power of [?], and sinners from transgression and from bitter wrath.
All this the great King Christ Jesus did by his own power.
And let no one suppose that it was only this, that he released only those who were under sin.
Rather, let him understand from this figure that he himself also blotted out sin and slew the power of sin, namely death.
And he set all free from sin and death and blotted out the power of death, which is its tyranny.
But whoever from now on brings forth from himself thoughts of deceit and sin, let him blame himself for his transgressions.
But it cannot prevent the resurrection, for the power of death has been abolished.
Yet this does not mean that those who sin and do not repent of their transgression will not be punished.
For it says thus: "He who led out those in bonds by his might, likewise those who embittered him and those who dwelt in tombs."
And it speaks not only of those who embitter, but also of those who became embittered and those whom they have embittered.
For at the resurrection of Christ many dead rose, who had been buried in tombs, for it says:
"Many of the saints rose and entered with him into the holy city of Jerusalem."
And their rising was a great wonder, by which the resurrection of the Lord was attested.
For those who rose were mature men, full of days, who knew how to give an answer and how to hear and understand a reply.
Some were about thirty years old and some twenty, and they were able to recognize one another, brother his brother, father his son, and son his father.
And their relatives and acquaintances would ask each one of those who had risen: "Are you the one of such a name?"
And they would answer: "That is my name." And they would say: "I have risen from the tomb of this place and have come, and you are called by this name."
And they would ask: "Where have you come from?" They would answer: "We rose and came."
And they would respond to one another, son to father and father to son: "What happened, or how did you rise?"
Those who had risen answered and said to them: "What deed was done among you three days ago?" And the people of Israel was undone and [?].
They answered and said to those who had risen: "What matter are you speaking of? Nothing has happened here."
Those who had risen answered: "Do you not know that the earth shook, and the abysses were stirred up, and the lower depths of hell were overthrown?
And you, what were you doing on that day, or what was that deed?" And they recalled it and said: "A certain deceiver, who was called Jesus, we seized
and crucified." But those who had risen raised their voices and said: "Woe to you!
He it was who came to us, and overthrew the walls of hell, and cut the bonds of death by his power, and raised us from our graves.
And that saying has been fulfilled which says: 'The dead shall rise, and all who dwell in the tombs shall be raised up.'"
And the Lord of life would show that the bonds of the souls confined in hell were cut by his power, through his descent into hell,
so that no one might say that he brought up only souls from hell. For this reason he raised many bodies of the saints, giving them back their souls.
They came and entered this city of Jerusalem; and those who had been embittered, whose souls had been confined in hell and whose bodies in the tombs, having risen
in soul and body, went into the city and appeared to many, and reminded those who had embittered the Lord, and those who had seized their Lord and tormented him.
These were witnesses of his resurrection. Well appointed is the stone beryl, which is dark, blood-colored and [?],
and which resembles the blood-stained garment of Joseph, which his brothers smeared with blood and sent to their father Jacob.
Well, moreover, were the colors of the stone beryl recorded; they signify the quietness, gentleness and purity of Joseph,
who by wisdom attained to rule and authority, and to being beloved by Pharaoh and the Egyptians and the whole world,
just as the stone beryl is set in the crowns of rulers, and is set in the crowns and ornaments of noble women, and is also inserted in the rings of sovereigns and grandees.
And the stone beryl adorns all, for it is an honor to all; all this meaning is to be seen in the stone beryl.
I shall now begin to speak of the twelfth stone, for it is the gathering and completion of all the stones that are set upon the oracle and that tablet of judgment.
12. The stone onyx. The twelfth stone is onyx. And its color is deep red.
And this stone is pleasing to the daughters of rulers, and to the rich and the powerful. And they make it into drinking cups and do not part with it.
There is also another onyx stone like this one, whose own color is white, like pure-colored [?] and like marble.
And in it many colors are spread out, resembling purple.
And its appearance is beautiful, and it is of such [?] that one can make a drinking cup of it, whatever the size. But we do not find the place from which it comes.
But we have heard this much: that it is found in the land of India, in Ethiopia, and in the region of the Thebaid, and in many other places as well.
Wonderful is this stone, on which was carved, engraved and written the name of Benjamin, the last in order after the sons of Israel.
For just as he is the youngest of the sons of Jacob, so also this stone is the last and the end of the oracle breastplate.
Benjamin was the youngest, and before all others he reigned over Israel, for Saul, the son of Kish, was of the tribe of Benjamin,
who first reigned over the sons of Israel; and judges were appointed from this tribe, who judged Israel like kings.
And other rulers and mighty men also arose from this tribe, from among whom Saul became king, until the reign of David, who was of the tribe of Judah.
And after the Babylonian captivity many from that tribe arose who delivered Israel.
Of the tribe of Benjamin was Esther, the daughter of Aminadab, the brother of Mordecai's father.
Of this tribe also was Mordecai, the son of Jair; and they were great men, and leaders and teachers of Israel.
From the tribe of Benjamin Saul first appeared as king, who delivered Israel from its enemies.
And after the Babylonian captivity Esther was of the tribe of Benjamin, through whom the captives were delivered.
Truly wondrous is the appearance of the onyx stone. It is further mentioned in the Law as a fragrant incense, when you compound the scents of the ointments
and burn the incenses, and they say: This is the incense: onyx, stacte, and galbanum and onyx.
There is also another onyx, when someone compounds fragrant ointments
and for the mixture you prepare a shell of onyx stone; and when they are poured into it, those fragrant ointments are blended.
And now, so that we may not prolong the telling of its whole nature, lingering for a long time to speak about the onyx and the incenses and the ointments,
I will now pass over this place in silence and begin to expound the others, one after another.
The name of Benjamin was fittingly written on the onyx stone, for onyx is beloved of the radiant [?] ones;
and to brides it was greatly beloved, truly because of its quietness and gentleness; for he was a support and a guardian to him and to his brother Joseph.
Truly Joseph rightly loved Benjamin, and gave him five portions more than his brothers.
Benjamin was beloved of his father and of his brothers, for he himself and his tribe were archers and warriors, and in many places they delivered Israel.
Benjamin was also beloved of God, for Jerusalem fell to him as a portion of inheritance, where the temple and the altar were built and where acceptable sacrifices were offered to God.
This one was first established as king, and he relinquished that power to Judah.
And after the captivity deliverers came to appear from the tribe of Levi over the people of Israel.
Truly, after all the apostles, Paul the apostle appeared as one chosen, from the tribe of Benjamin.
Just as Benjamin was the last of all the brothers, so also this one was chosen last; and as Benjamin was beloved of all,
like the onyx stone, so also Paul the apostle was beautiful and beloved to the churches and to all the faithful, a "chosen vessel."
And as the prtskhili [?] stone is beloved by kings and brides, and they fashion from it a cup for their drinking,
so truly Paul, shown forth by God as apostle of the holy bride of Christ, which is the Church,
holds out that spiritual cup which was granted to him by God.
And the book of the Apostle and the apostolic writings are read at one time in the year,
but the book of Paul, on all days and at all hours, waters and satisfies the Church of God with that spiritual cup.
This is the portion of Benjamin, five times greater than the portions of his brothers. And then that cup of Joseph was found in Benjamin's sack, where it had been placed.
This is what Samuel the prophet said to King Saul, who was of the tribe of Benjamin: "Yours are the good things of Israel and of your father's house."
What, then, are those good things of Israel? They are the holy counsels which were shown forth by Paul the apostle.
Truly the gifts and treasures and all the good things of the house of Israel were offered to Saul, that king of Israel.
But Paul shows this of himself to a still greater degree: "Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they kindred of Abraham?
So am I." And then he says: "A Hebrew of Hebrews, of the race of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin, as to the law a Pharisee.
And I became a zealot for the law of the fathers." And there is also the rest, which he says one thing after another, and for this reason it is written about him.
And in the hundred and sixteenth psalm he says: "I believed what I was saying." He became a fellow singer with David.
Paul the apostle says in his own letters: "And we too have believed, for which reason we speak."
Here David has said this concerning this figure, and it was fulfilled spiritually in Paul, for he said: "I too believe, for which reason I speak, that which we believe."
When he was going to Damascus, the Lord appeared to him from heaven and said to him: "Saul, Saul, why have you set yourself to persecute me?"
And Saul said to him: "Who are you, Lord?" Christ said to him: "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting."
And after this he said to him: "Go into the city, and there you will be told what it is fitting for you to do."
And then he says: "He got up and could not see. They took me by the hand, and I went into the city." This is what that psalm passage says next:
"And I was greatly humbled," for earlier he says: "Mounted on chariots, with great arrogance and self-conceit, I set out."
"And like a beggar I am led in by the hand, for formerly my mind was darkened, for I was a fighter against God.
But now God has darkened my eyes, that he may instruct me, and that the eyes of my heart may be opened and I may come to the knowledge of God."
Truly this is what David says: "And I was greatly humbled." God instructed me, removed my rash impulses far from me, humbled me, and revealed his terror upon me.
I am astonished, and I know it, and now I enter Damascus led by the hand, concerning which he also says: "I said in my amazement that every man is a liar."
Truly it is astonishing, for formerly he was in chariots and now he is led by the hand like a beggar; then Saul, and now Paul.
First a persecutor, and now an apostle. Truly it is fitting for me to say:
"I said in my amazement that every man is a liar," for everything I heard in Jerusalem was false.
I brought letters from them so that I might in some way help those high priests, for you were surely lying when you said
that the disciples had stolen away the one who rose, and they called the Lord a man, and they called the one who turns back those who have gone astray a deceiver.
Truly, in that fall of mine and in my blindness, I said: all men are liars,
for he who died and was buried and was stolen away by the disciples, how now did he speak to me from heaven and say [?], so that it was only talk [?].
This blindness of the eyes convinces and enlightens minds that have been blinded.
And after this, when he entered Damascus and his eyes were given light, he believed in our Lord Jesus Christ, and he spoke and preached the way of truth.
And after all this he received from the Lord, in exchange for those wicked deeds, [?] stripped bare in good judgments [?], and he gave thanks and said:
"What shall I give back to the Lord for all that he has given me?" I was a persecutor: he made me worthy of apostleship.
I was a blasphemer: he made me worthy of the divine visions of heaven. I was living in error through ignorance: he revealed to me great and awesome counsels.
And he says: "What shall I give back to the Lord for all this that he has given me?"
What indeed can compare as a repayment for the death of the Son of God, except only that cup which our Lord Jesus Christ drank?
Now, "I will take that cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord." This is what he means when he says:
I will take the death of Christ upon myself, the cup about which the Lord spoke to his own disciples: "The cup that I am to drink, are you indeed able to drink it?"
And desiring this, Paul said: "I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord." And he says: "Even if it be unto death,
even if sorrows come for the sake of the name of the Lord, I will not deny it, neither in prosperity nor in distress, nor will I abandon or depart from the name of the Most High."
And that this is so is shown by the saying that follows:
"Precious before the Lord is the death of his saints," and the other thing that he says next after it.
Truly good and beautiful to watchful eyes is the cup that was handed to the bride, who is the Church.
She drew it [?] and brought forth from his own tribe of Benjamin Paul, who gave the cup of the knowledge of God and of joy to all the ends of the heavens to drink.
And a fivefold portion was given to him for his labor, as to Benjamin, for he says thus: "Five times I also suffered."
[?] For he ran to receive five times the labor of one man, as he himself says: "I toiled more than all."
And so as not to give praise to himself, he says: "Not I, but the grace that was given to me."
Truly "Benjamin is a ravening wolf, who in the morning ate his food and in the evening prepared it" and gathered it [?].
Renewed, Benjamin had become young again through the hand of Paul, for in his youth Paul snatched like a wolf and tore the bones and flesh of many.
This is what it says: that he will eat food at dawn, and the same in the evening.
When he reached maturity, he took that spiritual food and spread out to everyone the teaching concerning God.
He who at one time slaughtered and destroyed those who were believers in Christ.
But afterward he poured himself out and nourished others, as he says: "I would spend and give myself."
And again it says there: "Benjamin, a wondrous youth," as the divine books say.
And it does not say only "Benjamin" there; not only "Benjamin," but it also says "youth" there. And who is it that says this?
That is, the youngest of his brothers. But of the kindred of that Benjamin, Paul became young by falling [?]. And afterward he became a chosen apostle.
And this divine sign did not appear to him right there in Jerusalem, but on his journey to Damascus, for there it says: "Benjamin, wondrous in his youth."
So also Paul, trembling and astonished, said, "Who are you, Lord?" A voice came to Paul and said: "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting."
And he was astonished by the great teaching. He cast away foolishness and arrogance and received the grace of wisdom from the Holy Spirit.
He became a chosen vessel and a teacher of the churches. This is what it says: "There is Benjamin, a youth to be marveled at."
Come and see this manifold wonder, how beautiful to behold is that bride fittingly adorned, the Church,
which is from the graces of the divine Spirit, as it says in the Song of Songs, which is this Blessing of Blessings:
"Your neck is like the iron middle of a lampstand, and like purple resembling ivory."
"Your lips are as if woven; the tips of your fingers are like the tips of the trees of Lebanon, which looks directly toward the regions of Damascus."
Now, fitted together with one another, these words are interpreted thus: it showed Christ as the head, the apostles as the lips, and the two Laws as the eyes.
The sense of smell is this: that the holy apostles received the breath of fragrance and spread it through all the world, and they said:
"We are the breath of the fragrance of Christ: to some a living fragrance leading to life, and to others a deadly one leading to death."
And also the other thing, which it says next in sequence: "The tips of your fingers are like the tips of Lebanon."
For Lebanon is near Damascus. It appears [?] that this was not said about the beauty of women.
For length in the tips of the fingernails, like the tips of those trees, is very unsightly.
For this is said about the Church and with regard to the apostles, for Paul received letters from the high priests and was going to Damascus, near the foot of Lebanon.
And teaching and the breath of fragrance were given to him from heaven, and he heard the name of the Lord Jesus.
This is what it says: "Your name is an ointment of fragrance poured out."
And grace was granted to Paul through the name of Christ; he spread abroad the grace of fragrance and filled all the ends of heaven with the teaching of fragrance.
With great beauty the onyx stone, on which the name of Benjamin was written, has gladdened us,
for it was the end and completion of the stones set in four rows, which were carved, engraved, and set upon that tablet of judgment.
As far as I was able, I have set forth the finding and the appearance of these precious stones, as your honor requested.
Although these commands given to me were great and beyond me, I have laid love and obedience before you.
Now may your courage accept and receive this timidity of my mind.
And if anything has been left out or is lacking, may it be filled up by your all-loving and generous wisdom, for love endures all things.
"Love believes in all things, hopes in all things. It does not please itself. Love is not arrogant."
"Love is not ashamed, but love is in all things by every means," because it has power from the divine side. And now glory to God from every side.
Although this understanding wisdom of ours was deficient, by these commands of yours these minds of ours have been made all the wiser.
Although we were ignorant of what these commands of yours concerned, those twelve stones, the light of knowledge has shone upon us.
If translating a word from the language of the Romans into the language of the Greeks requires great wisdom, how much more is this so for me,
to whom it has fallen, for the sake of your love, to expound the counsels of God that were hidden in the Law.
Truly you commanded me to undertake what is beyond my ability.
Although it was exceedingly excessive and beyond my mind, it was granted by the Lord God and through your prayers, for the benefit of us and of many.
The honor of your love has become an example for us.
Now in every way may the Father be glorified through the Son and the Son through the Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.
The eleventh arrangement of the number, and the division of the sons of Israel, as Moses commanded the twelve tribes to stand:
six of the tribes on Mount Gerizim and the other six on Mount Ebal, as is written in Deuteronomy.
And the division of the tribes is as follows, for it says thus: Let six stand on Mount Gerizim.
These are the ones who speak the blessings, and they said: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, Benjamin. And on Mount Ebal,
those who spoke the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, Naphtali.
This was not said as an arrangement for writing down the ordered stones that were on the tablet of the oracle.
But let us call to mind that eleventh arrangement of the numbers, which was divided in two:
six on the one mountain and six on the other. This we have found: that they were set upon the two emerald stones.
The names of the sons of Israel were written on these shoulder-pieces, because the twelve names could not have been written together on a single emerald stone. Instead they were divided:
six tribes were written on one stone and six on the other.
The six tribes for the blessing on Gerizim were written on the stone that was on the right shoulder-piece, and the six tribes for the curse on Ebal were written
on the stone that was on the left shoulder-piece. These mountains are opposite Jericho, on the east side, near Gilgal.
The books tell us this about the place where the sons of Israel were blessed. Those who were on Mount Gerizim and spoke the blessings were:
Simeon, Levi, Judah and the other three with them. They spoke thus: "Blessed is he who does the will of the Lord."
And the sound of the response could be heard in the plains where the people stood. And they said: "So be it! So be it!"
And then Reuben, Gad, Asher and Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali were on Mount Ebal, and they spoke thus: "Cursed be everyone who does not do what is written in these books of the law!"
And all the people say: "So be it! So be it!" And "Amen" is translated "So be it."
For the voice from the two mountains and the response of the two companies could be heard by the people who stood in the plain between the two mountains.
And in translation Mount Gerizim is called "mountain of deliverance," and Mount Ebal "defiled and polluted."
But some people, who have read the divine books without understanding, think otherwise, above all the race of the Samaritans:
they say that Mount Gerizim is something else, namely the high mountain that rises above Sikima, which is Shechem, the mountain that is opposite Shechem, the city of the Samaritans.
This is the city the Lord entered, and from it the Samaritan woman came out and saw the Lord, for he was sitting by the well.
And Shechem is now called Neapolis. It is a rich and populous city in the land of the Palestinians, and at that time Samaritans and Jews lived in it.
And they are called Samaritans because the mountain near that city was called the mountain of Somer, and he had a son and called his name Someron.
The mountain too was given the name Somer. Because of this the race of the Samaritans received its name.
And the race of the Samaritans came from the land of the Babylonians and the Assyrians.
Nebuchadnezzar had brought them and settled them in the land of the Galileans and the Palestinians.
When Nebuchadnezzar took the sons of Israel captive, the elders of the sons of Israel went in before King Nebuchadnezzar.
And the men who went in before King Nebuchadnezzar were Ezra, others from among the priests, and elders of the sons of Israel.
And they begged Nebuchadnezzar to send men to guard their land, so that the land would not turn into forest and be overthrown and ruined.
And Nebuchadnezzar heard their request. He chose his own servants from four peoples and sent them to guard their land.
And these were the names of the peoples who went to settle in the land of Israel: the Kudaeans, the Cuthaeans, the Sepharvaeans and the Anagonaeans.
And each of these peoples had its own idols, which they worshipped and called gods. They came and settled near Mount Somer.
And from the name of that mountain and from their own deeds they were called Samaritans, for guarding is called "somer," "mter" [?].
For these were guards of that land, and in those times lions and leopards and bears had multiplied against those guards over Samaria.
They were destroying them, and those beasts had multiplied so greatly that day by day they were finishing off the people of Samaria.
And they sent to cry out to King Nebuchadnezzar, asking that he remove them from that land of the Galileans and that they might return there to their own land,
so that the whole of that people might not be wiped out by the multitude of the beasts.
And Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and said: How then did those people of Israel live there?
He summoned the elders of the sons of Israel and asked them: How were you able to live in that land?
And they gave a true and right answer and said to Nebuchadnezzar: None of the nations is able to live there,
unless he has the law of the Lord God, and unless he walks in accordance with the law and serves the Lord God.
And Nebuchadnezzar requested that law from the elders, and they wrote it out according to their own law and gave it to him.
And Nebuchadnezzar ordered that the law be sent to those Samaritans by the hand of Ezra the priest.
This is not that Ezra who belonged to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, but another Ezra, who is his namesake.
And this Ezra had been a priest in that land of Israel.
He gave those Samaritans only the five books of Scripture, written in that first script, according to the form that the Lord gave on Mount Sinai.
And the sons of the Hebrews name that form of writing "diesinon," which is translated "the set-up tablets."
But the form of writing that the Hebrews have now is not like that earlier writing which was written on those tablets.
Rather, the one that the Jews now have is called "somoronos."
For that of the Samaritans is called "desinon," which in those times was written on those hewn tablets. And Ezra the priest went away from Babylon.
He wished to separate the people of the Israelites from the Samaritans, lest those Samaritans mingle with that race of Abraham, for they held the law of Moses.
He did not change the desinon writing of the books of the prophets, but only that of the Scripture,
which those Samaritans had received as their natural law, so that by this he might separate from each other the race of Abraham and the race of the Samaritans.

Now I have extended and lingered over the account of all this and have investigated where the Samaritans come from, or from which peoples, and how the name was given them from the name of that mountain and of the son of Somer,
who was of the race of the Canaanites and Perizzites, or how the name of the Samaritans is translated "guard," for they were guards of that land.
I will begin to speak further in another way and will show them openly: how they were guards of that law and yet served idols.
For it is written thus concerning the Samaritans: that they were trained [?] and taught, and they had the law of the Lord God, and they worshipped their own idols.
But in the law of the Lord it is written: "You shall not worship idols."
And if someone worships idols, how could he be found to be a fulfiller of the law?
But those four foul tribes of the Samaritans acted with guile when they heard that Ezra was coming to destroy and crush those idols,
as it is written in the law of Moses, for God commanded that everyone who worships idols should be stoned with stones.
When the tribe of the Samaritans heard this, they hurried and took those idols down from the height of the steps of their temple, and carried off their idols and hid them on Mount Gerizim,
as it is written, one after another, in the narratives. As it says: the men of Babylon had their idols, Succoth and Benoth, and the men of Cuth had their idols,
whose name was Nergal, and the men of Hamath had the idols Ashima, and the Avvites had the idols Nibhaz and Tartak, and the idols Sepharvaim.
And through that error the hearts of those Samaritans were turned to worship toward Mount Gerizim, where those idols had been concealed and hidden, and on every side,
wherever they are, they worship toward that mountain, from north and south, from every side, wherever they are, they worship the idols, for these were on Gerizim,
so that the word of the scripture might be fulfilled which says that those Samaritans stood and waited upon the law of the Lord.
But they worship their own idols, for those who are Samaritans now do not know where those idols are hidden, and they say
that "our fathers worshipped on this mountain," and they declare themselves to be offspring of Joseph.
And all this happened so that the word of that scripture might all the more not be proved false.
For, in keeping with their deeds, the divine books speak of their keeping the law of the Lord and of their worshipping their own idols.
And this whole narrative was composed concerning those twelve tribes that were divided on Mount Gerizim and Ebal.
And we have shown that this is not the Gerizim that the Samaritans worship.
And they have gone astray through deception, for they do not know all the divine books, but know only the books of Genesis and do not read the other books.
And they suppose that it is that mountain which is near Neapolis, for that Mount Gerizim is great and high.
And there is that one mountain which lies opposite it, of which they say in error that this is Ebal,
for Shechem and the place where Joseph is laid are between those two mountains, in the middle of the valley, with the mountains on this side and on that.
And on one side of Mount Gerizim steps have been made up to the very summit of the mountain of the Samaritans, who had settled in the city of Neapolis.
And on the summit of the mountain they made a building for it, and they worship on Mount Gerizim, as we said before, out of their error and not out of wisdom.
For the scriptures and all the narratives that are true refute them, for the summit of that mountain is high.

And if someone should cry out on the top of that mountain, there is no way that the voice could be heard from above in those plains; and when those six tribal chiefs cried out and spoke those blessings to the people,
Those who would not hear that voice because of the height of the mountain, how could they have said "Amen," which in translation is "So be it"?
For its height is more than one mile, since there are many steps up to the summit. As they say, the steps number one thousand five hundred and more.
And at the lower foot of the mountain there is a place that has no steps. From such a height, how could a voice be heard by those
who stood at the foot of the mountain, or, by those above, the voice of those standing below?
By all this the error of those Samaritans is refuted. For these are not the mountains of which the children of Israel spoke.
Now the book of Joshua son of Nun, which was written after the book of Genesis, shows us concerning the blessings and the curses
that on the eastern side, opposite Jericho, stand the two mountains, Ebal and Gerizim,
and near the place called Gilgal, where the twelve stones were set up, where also Joshua son of Nun kept the Passover and they ate the bread of that land,
where the manna ceased from them. In this place the children of Israel were circumcised with a sword of flint.
This is the place "Gilgal, which stands on the eastern side of Jericho." Near it stand those mountains,
which are small hills, Gerizim and Ebal, upon which they pronounced the curses and blessings.
But the great mountain Gerizim, which is Shechem, stands on the southern side, near Jericho, on the side of the sunrise, and is fifty-two miles distant from Jericho.
But these mountains, Ebal and Gerizim, are near Jericho, about two miles away to the east, close to the southern side.
Now let us make these mountains known in all truth. Here let it be enough only to say and to understand all this.
